verses.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. \b
No the earth as formless and void, and darkness as over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God as hovering over the surface of the aters. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let there be light,” and there as light.
And God sa that the light as good, and He separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light “ day,” and the darkness He called “ night.” \b \pmo And there as evening, and there as morning— the first day. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let there be an expanse beteen the aters, to separate the aters from the aters.”
So God made the expanse and separated the aters beneath it from the aters above. And it as so.
God called the expanse “ sky.” \b \pmo And there as evening, and there as morning— the second day. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let the aters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it as so.
God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of aters He called “ seas.” And God sa that it as good. \b \pmo
Then God said, “ Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit ith seed according to its kind.” And it as so.
The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit ith seed according to their kinds. And God sa that it as good. \b \pmo
And there as evening, and there as morning— the third day. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish beteen the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.
And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it as so. \b \pmo
God made to great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as ell. \b \pmo
God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,
to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God sa that it as good. \b \pmo
And there as evening, and there as morning— the fourth day. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let the aters teem ith living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, ith hich the aters teemed according to their kinds, and every bird of flight after its kind. And God sa that it as good. \b \pmo
Then God blessed them and said, “ Be fruitful and multiply and fill the aters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.” \b \pmo
And there as evening, and there as morning— the fifth day. \b \pmo
And God said, “ Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land cralers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it as so.
God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crals upon the earth according to its kind. And God sa that it as good. \b \pmo

Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crals upon it.” \b
So God created man in His on image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. \b \pmo

God blessed them and said to them, “ Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crals upon the earth.” \b \pmo
Then God said, “ Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree hose fruit contains seed. They ill be yours for food.

And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crals upon the earth— everything that has the breath of life in it— I have given every green plant for food.” And it as so. \b \pmo
And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it as very good. \b \pmo And there as evening, and there as morning— the sixth day.
Thus the heavens and the earth ere completed in all their vast array.
And by the seventh day God had finished the ork He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His ork. \b
Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the ork of creation that He had accomplished. \b
This is the account of the heavens and the earth hen they ere created, in the day that the LORD God made them. \b
No no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted; for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there as no man to cultivate the ground.
But springs elled up from the earth and atered the hole surface of the ground. \b
Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being. \b
And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, here He placed the man He had formed.

Out of the ground the LORD God gave groth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden ere the tree of life and the tree of the knoledge of good and evil. \b
No a river floed out of Eden to ater the garden, and from there it branched into four headaters: \b \li1
The name of the first river is Pishon; it inds through the hole land of Havilah, here there is gold.
And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there. \b \li1
The name of the second river is Gihon; it inds through the hole land of Cush. \b \li1
The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it runs along the east side of Assyria. \b \li1 And the fourth river is the Euphrates. \b
Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it. \b
And the LORD God commanded him, “ You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,
but you must not eat from the tree of the knoledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you ill surely die.” \b
The LORD God also said, “ It is not good for the man to be alone. I ill make for him a suitable helper.” \b

And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see hat he ould name each one. And hatever the man called each living creature, that as its name.
The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper as found. \b
So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and hile he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area ith flesh.
And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a oman and brought her to him.
And the man said: \b “ This is no bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ’oman,’ for out of man she as taken.” \b
For this reason a man ill leave his father and mother and be united to his ife, and they ill become one flesh. \b
And the man and his ife ere both naked, and they ere not ashamed.
No the serpent as more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the oman, “ Did God really say, ’ You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’” \b
The oman ansered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden,
but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ’ You must not eat of it or touch it, or you ill die.’” \b
“ You ill not surely die,” the serpent told her.
“ For God knos that in the day you eat of it, your eyes ill be opened and you ill be like God, knoing good and evil.” \b

When the oman sa that the tree as good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it as desirable for obtaining isdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband ho as ith her, and he ate it. \b
And the eyes of both of them ere opened, and they kne that they ere naked; so they seed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves. \b
Then the man and his ife heard the voice of the LORD God alking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden. \b
But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?” \b
“ I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “ and I as afraid because I as naked; so I hid myself.” \b
“ Who told you that you ere naked?” asked the LORD God. “ Have you eaten from the tree of hich I commanded you not to eat?” \b
And the man ansered, “ The oman hom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.” \b
Then the LORD God said to the oman, “ What is this you have done?” \b \b

So the LORD God said to the serpent: \b “ Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly ill you go, and dust you ill eat, all the days of your life.
And I ill put enmity beteen you and the oman, and beteen your seed and her seed. He ill crush your head, and you ill strike his heel.” \b
To the oman He said: \b “ I ill sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you ill bring forth children. Your desire ill be for your husband, and he ill rule over you.” \b

And to Adam He said: \b “ Because you have listened to the voice of your ife and have eaten from the tree of hich I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you ill eat of it all the days of your life.
Both thorns and thistles it ill yield for you, and you ill eat the plants of the field.
By the seat of your bro you ill eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it ere you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.” \b
And Adam named his ife Eve, because she ould be the mother of all the living. \b
And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his ife, and He clothed them. \b
Then the LORD God said, “ Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knoing good and evil. And no, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...” \b
Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to ork the ground from hich he had been taken.
So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along ith a hirling sord of flame to guard the ay to the tree of life.
And Adam had relations ith his ife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. \b \b
Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel. \b
So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,
hile Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. \b
but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell. \b
“ Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “ and hy has your countenance fallen?
If you do hat is right, ill you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do hat is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.” \b
Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “ Let us go out to the field.” And hile they ere in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him. \b
And the LORD said to Cain, “ Where is your brother Abel?” \b \b
“ What have you done?” replied the LORD. “ The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
No you are cursed and banished from the ground, hich has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the ground, it ill no longer yield its produce to you. You ill be a fugitive and a anderer on the earth.” \b
But Cain said to the LORD, “ My punishment is greater than I can bear.
Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I ill be hidden; I ill be a fugitive and a anderer on the earth, and hoever finds me ill kill me.” \b
“ Not so!” replied the LORD. “ If anyone slays Cain, then Cain ill be avenged sevenfold.” And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one ho found him ould kill him. \b
So Cain ent out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden. \b
And Cain had relations ith his ife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch. \b
No to Enoch as born Irad, and Irad as the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael as the father of Methusael, and Methusael as the father of Lamech.
And Lamech married to omen, one named Adah and the other Zillah. \b
Adah gave birth to Jabal; he as the father of those ho dell in tents and raise livestock.
And his brother’s name as Jubal; he as the father of all ho play the harp and flute. \b
And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain as Naamah. \b
Then Lamech said to his ives: \b “ Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; ives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for ounding me, a young man for striking me.
If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.” \b
And Adam again had relations ith his ife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.” \b
And to Seth also a son as born, and he called him Enosh. \b
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His on likeness.
Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they ere created, He called them “ man.” \b
When Adam as 130 years old, he had a son in his on likeness, after his on image; and he named him Seth.
And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died. \b
When Seth as 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died. \b
When Enosh as 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died. \b
When Kenan as 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died. \b
When Mahalalel as 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died. \b
When Jared as 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died. \b
When Enoch as 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch alked ith God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Enoch lived a total of 365 years. \b
Enoch alked ith God, and then he as no more, because God had taken him aay. \b
When Methuselah as 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died. \b
When Lamech as 182 years old, he had a son.
And he named him Noah, saying, “ May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.”
And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died. \b
After Noah as 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
No hen men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters ere born to them,
the sons of God sa that the daughters of men ere beautiful, and they took as ives homever they chose. \b
So the LORD said, “ My Spirit ill not contend ith man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.” \b

The Nephilim ere on the earth in those days— and afterard as ell— hen the sons of God had relations ith the daughters of men. And they bore them children ho became the mighty men of old, men of renon. \b
Then the LORD sa that the ickedness of man as great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart as altogether evil all the time.
And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He as grieved in His heart.
So the LORD said, “ I ill blot out man, hom I have created, from the face of the earth— every man and beast and craling creature and bird of the air— for I am grieved that I have made them.” \b
Noah, hoever, found favor in the eyes of the LORD. \b
This is the account of Noah. Noah as a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah alked ith God.
And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. \b
No the earth as corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
And God looked upon the earth and sa that it as corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ays. \b
Then God said to Noah, “ The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. No behold, I ill destroy both them and the earth. \b
Make for yourself an ark of gopher ood; make rooms in the ark and coat it ith pitch inside and out.
And this is ho you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits ide, and 30 cubits high.
You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its alls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build loer, middle, and upper decks. \b
And behold, I ill bring floodaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth ill perish.
But I ill establish My covenant ith you, and you ill enter the ark— you and your sons and your ife and your sons’ ives ith you. \b
And you are to bring to of every living creature into the ark— male and female— to keep them alive ith you.
To of every kind of bird and animal and craling creature ill come to you to be kept alive.
You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.” \b
So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
Then the LORD said to Noah, “ Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
You are to take ith you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.
For seven days from no I ill send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I ill ipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.” \b
And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him. \b
No Noah as 600 years old hen the floodaters came upon the earth.
And Noah and his ife, ith his sons and their ives, entered the ark to escape the aters of the flood.
The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crals along the ground
came to Noah to enter the ark, to by to, male and female, as God had commanded Noah. \b
And after seven days the floodaters came upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens ere opened.
And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. \b
On that very day Noah entered the ark, along ith his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his ife, and the three ives of his sons—
they and every kind of ild animal, livestock, craling creature, bird, and inged creature.
They came to Noah to enter the ark, to by to of every creature ith the breath of life.
And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in. \b
For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the aters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.
So the aters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the aters.
Finally, the aters completely inundated the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens ere covered. \b
The aters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished— birds, livestock, animals, every creature that sarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
Of all that as on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.

And every living thing on the face of the earth as destroyed— man and livestock, craling creatures and birds of the air; they ere blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those ith him in the ark remained. \b
And the aters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.
But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that ere ith him in the ark. And God sent a ind over the earth, and the aters began to subside.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens ere closed, and the rain from the sky as restrained.
The aters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the aters had gone don. \b
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
And the aters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible. \b
After forty days Noah opened the indo he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the aters had dried up from the earth. \b
Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the aters had receded from the surface of the ground.

But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the aters ere still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark. \b
Noah aited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening ith a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah kne that the aters had receded from the earth. \b
And Noah aited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him. \b

In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the aters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and sa that the surface of the ground as dry.
By the tenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth as fully dry. \b
Then God said to Noah,
“ Come out of the ark, you and your ife, along ith your sons and their ives.
Bring out all the living creatures that are ith you— birds, livestock, and everything that crals upon the ground— so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.” \b
So Noah came out, along ith his sons and his ife and his sons’ ives.
Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird— everything that moves upon the earth— came out of the ark, kind by kind. \b
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.

When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “ Never again ill I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again ill I destroy all living creatures as I have done. \b
As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and inter, day and night shall never cease.”
And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “ Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

The fear and dread of you ill fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crals on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.
Everything that lives and moves ill be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I no give you all things.
But you must not eat meat ith its lifeblood still in it.
And surely I ill require the life of any man or beast by hose hand your lifeblood is shed. I ill demand an accounting from anyone ho takes the life of his fello man: \b
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood ill be shed; for in His on image God has made mankind.
But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it.” \b
Then God said to Noah and his sons ith him,
“ Behold, I no establish My covenant ith you and your descendants after you,
and ith every living creature that as ith you— the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth— every living thing that came out of the ark.
And I establish My covenant ith you: Never again ill all life be cut off by the aters of a flood; never again ill there be a flood to destroy the earth.” \b
And God said, “ This is the sign of the covenant I am making beteen Me and you and every living creature ith you, a covenant for all generations to come:
I have set My rainbo in the clouds, and it ill be a sign of the covenant beteen Me and the earth. \b
Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbo appears in the clouds,
I ill remember My covenant beteen Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again ill the aters become a flood to destroy all life.
And henever the rainbo appears in the clouds, I ill see it and remember the everlasting covenant beteen God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth.” \b
So God said to Noah, “ This is the sign of the covenant that I have established beteen Me and every creature on the earth.” \b
The sons of Noah ho came out of the ark ere Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And Ham as the father of Canaan.
These three ere the sons of Noah, and from them the hole earth as populated. \b
No Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.
But hen he drank some of its ine, he became drunk and uncovered himself inside his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, sa his father’s nakedness and told his to brothers outside. \b

Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and alking backard, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces ere turned aay so that they did not see their father’s nakedness. \b
When Noah aoke from his drunkenness and learned hat his youngest son had done to him,
he said, \b “Cursed be Canaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.” \b
He also declared: \b “ Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem.
May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant.” \b
After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.
So Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.
This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, ho also had sons after the flood. \b
The sons of Japheth: \b \pmo Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. \b
The sons of Gomer: \b \pmo Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. \b
And the sons of Javan: \b \pmo Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.
From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans ithin their nations. \b
The sons of Ham: \b \pmo Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. \b
The sons of Cush: \b \pmo Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. \b \b \pmo Sheba and Dedan. \b
Cush as the father of Nimrod, ho began to be a mighty one on the earth.
He as a mighty hunter before the LORD; so it is said, “ Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”
His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he ent forth into Assyria, here he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
and Resen, hich is beteen Nineveh and the great city of Calah. \b
Mizraim as the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,
the Pathrusites, the Casluhites ( from hom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites. \b
And Canaan as the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. \b
and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toard Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toard Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha. \b
These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations. \b
And sons ere also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem as the forefather of all the sons of Eber. \b
The sons of Shem: \b \pmo Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. \b
The sons of Aram: \b \pmo Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash. \b
Arphaxad as the father of Shelah, and Shelah as the father of Eber. \b
To sons ere born to Eber: One as named Peleg, because in his days the earth as divided, and his brother as named Joktan. \b
And Joktan as the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these ere sons of Joktan.

The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.
And place inside the ark the Testimony, hich I ill give you. \b
And you are to construct a mercy seat of pure gold, to and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half ide.
Make to cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,
one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.
And the cherubim are to have ings that spread upard, overshadoing the mercy seat. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toard the mercy seat. \b
Set the mercy seat atop the ark, and put the Testimony that I ill give you into the ark. \b
And I ill meet ith you there above the mercy seat, beteen the to cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony; I ill speak ith you about all that I command you regarding the Israelites. \b
You are also to make a table of acacia ood to cubits long, a cubit ide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it ith pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
And make a rim around it a handbreadth ide and put a gold molding on the rim. \b
Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.
The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
Make the poles of acacia ood and overlay them ith gold, so that the table may be carried ith them. \b
You are also to make the plates and dishes, as ell as the pitchers and bols for pouring drink offerings. Make them out of pure gold. \b
And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times. \b
Then you are to make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. It shall be made of one piece, including its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals. \b
Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand— three on one side and three on the other.
There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each ith buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extend from the lampstand. \b
And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms ith buds and petals.
For the six branches that extend from the lampstand, a bud must be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
The buds and branches are to be all of one piece ith the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold. \b
Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it.
The ick trimmers and their trays must be of pure gold.
The lampstand and all these utensils shall be made from a talent of pure gold. \b
See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shon you on the mountain.
“ You are to construct the tabernacle itself ith ten curtains of finely spun linen, each ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully orked into them.
Each curtain shall be tenty-eight cubits long and four cubits ide — all curtains the same size. \b
Five of the curtains are to be joined together, and the other five joined as ell.
Make loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same for the end curtain in the second set. \b
Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops line up opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps as ell, and join the curtains together ith the clasps, so that the tabernacle ill be a unit. \b
You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle— eleven curtains in all.
Each of the eleven curtains is to be the same size— thirty cubits long and four cubits ide. \b
Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another. Then fold the sixth curtain over double at the front of the tent. \b
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps and put them through the loops to join the tent together as a unit. \b
As for the overlap that remains of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over shall hang don over the back of the tabernacle.
And the tent curtains ill be a cubit longer on either side, and the excess ill hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it. \b
Also make a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather. \b
You are to construct upright frames of acacia ood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half ide.
To tenons must be connected to each other for each frame. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this ay. \b
Construct tenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,
ith forty silver bases under the tenty frames— to bases for each frame, one under each tenon. \b
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make tenty frames
and forty silver bases— to bases under each frame. \b
Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the est side,
and to frames for the to back corners of the tabernacle,
coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. These ill serve as the to corners.
So there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases— to under each frame. \b
You are also to make five crossbars of acacia ood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the est. \b
The central crossbar in the middle of the frames shall extend from one end to the other.
Overlay the frames ith gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars ith gold. \b
So you are to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shon you on the mountain. \b
Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, ith cherubim skillfully orked into it.
Hang it ith gold hooks on four posts of acacia ood, overlaid ith gold and standing on four silver bases.
And hang the veil from the clasps and place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil. So the veil ill separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place. \b
Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
And place the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side. \b
For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
Make five posts of acacia ood for the curtain, overlay them ith gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.
“ You are to build an altar of acacia ood. The altar must be square, five cubits long, five cubits ide, and three cubits high.
Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it ith bronze. \b
Make all its utensils of bronze— its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bols, its meat forks, and its firepans.

Additionally, make poles of acacia ood for the altar and overlay them ith bronze.
The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on to sides of the altar hen it is carried. \b
Construct the altar ith boards so that it is hollo. It is to be made just as you ere shon on the mountain. \b
You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,

Likeise there are to be curtains on the north side, a hundred cubits long, ith tenty posts and tenty bronze bases, and ith silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The curtains on the est side of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits ide, ith ten posts and ten bases. \b
The east side of the courtyard, toard the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits ide.
Make the curtains on one side fifteen cubits long, ith three posts and three bases,
and the curtains on the other side fifteen cubits long, ith three posts and three bases. \b
The gate of the courtyard shall be tenty cubits long, ith a curtain embroidered ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It shall have four posts and four bases. \b
All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
The entire courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits ide, ith curtains of finely spun linen five cubits high, and ith bronze bases.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, including all its tent pegs and the tent pegs of the courtyard, shall be made of bronze. \b
And you are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually. \b

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.
“Next, have your brother Aaron brought to you from among the Israelites, along ith his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, to serve Me as priests.
Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to give him glory and splendor. \b
You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, hom I have filled ith a spirit of isdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration, so that he may serve Me as priest.

These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a oven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests.
They shall use gold, along ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen. \b
They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered ith gold, and ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
It shall have to shoulder pieces attached at to of its corners, so it can be fastened.
And the skillfully oven aistband of the ephod must be of one piece, of the same orkmanship— ith gold, ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and ith finely spun linen. \b
Take to onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:

Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear their names on his to shoulders as a memorial before the LORD. \b
Fashion gold filigree settings
and to chains of pure gold, made of braided cord ork; and attach these chains to the settings. \b
You are also to make a breastpiece of judgment ith the same orkmanship as the ephod. Construct it ith gold, ith blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and ith finely spun linen.

And mount on it a setting of gemstones, four ros of stones: \b \li1 In the first ro there shall be a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald; \b \li1
in the second ro a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; \b \li1
in the third ro a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; \b \li1
and in the fourth ro a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. \b
The telve stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal ith the name of one of the telve tribes. \b
For the breastpiece, make braided chains like cords of pure gold.
You are also to make to gold rings and fasten them to the to corners of the breastpiece.
Then fasten the to gold chains to the to gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and fasten the other ends of the to chains to the to filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front. \b
Make to more gold rings and attach them to the other to corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod. \b
Make to additional gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the to shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near its seam just above its oven aistband.
The rings of the breastpiece shall be tied to the rings of the ephod ith a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece is above the aistband of the ephod and does not sing out from the ephod. \b
Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he shall bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual reminder before the LORD. \b

And place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they ill also be over Aaron’s heart henever he comes before the LORD. Aaron ill continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD. \b
You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
ith an opening at its top in the center. Around the opening shall be a oven collar ith an opening like that of a garment, so that it ill not tear. \b
Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all the ay around the loer hem, ith gold bells beteen them,
alternating the gold bells and pomegranates around the loer hem of the robe. \b
Aaron must ear the robe henever he ministers, and its sound ill be heard hen he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he ill not die. \b
You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: \b \pc HOLY TO THE LORD. \b
Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

And it ill be orn on Aaron’s forehead, so that he may bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate ith regard to all their holy gifts. It shall alays be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD. \b
You are to eave the tunic ith fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.
Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons, to give them glory and splendor. \b
After you put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests. \b
Make linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, extending from aist to thigh.

Aaron and his sons must ear them henever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they ill not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.
“ No this is hat you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and to rams ithout blemish,
along ith unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed ith oil, and unleavened afers anointed ith oil. Make them out of fine heat flour,
put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along ith the bull and the to rams. \b
Then present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and ash them ith ater.
Take the garments and clothe Aaron ith the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him ith its oven aistband.
Put the turban on his head and attach the holy diadem to the turban.
Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head. \b
Present his sons as ell and clothe them ith tunics.
Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this ay you are to ordain Aaron and his sons. \b
You are to present the bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar ith your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys ith the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering. \b
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
You are to slaughter the ram, take its blood, and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, ash the entrails and legs, and place them ith its head and other pieces.
Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD. \b
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Sprinkle the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.

And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as ell as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments ill be consecrated, as ell as his sons and their garments. \b
Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys ith the fat on them, and the right thigh ( since this is a ram for ordination),
along ith one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made ith oil, and one afer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and ave them before the LORD as a ave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is an offering made by fire to the LORD. \b
Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and ave it before the LORD as a ave offering, and it ill be your portion.
Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the ave offering that is aved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
This ill belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites ill make to the LORD from their peace offerings. \b
The holy garments that belong to Aaron ill belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son ho succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must ear them for seven days. \b
You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
They must eat those things by hich atonement as made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.
And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred. \b
This is hat you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.
Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar ill become most holy; hatever touches the altar ill be holy. \b
This is hat you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: to lambs that are a year old.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at tilight.
With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed ith a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of ine.
And offer the second lamb at tilight ith the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD. \b
For the generations to come, this burnt offering shall be made regularly at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, here I ill meet you to speak ith you.
I ill also meet ith the Israelites there, and that place ill be consecrated by My glory.
So I ill consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I ill consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests. \b
Then I ill dell among the Israelites and be their God.
And they ill kno that I am the LORD their God, ho brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dell among them. \b
“ You are also to make an altar of acacia ood for the burning of incense.

Place the altar in front of the veil that is before the ark of the Testimony — before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony— here I ill meet ith you.

Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ When you take a census of the Israelites to number them, each man must pay the LORD a ransom for his life hen he is counted. Then no plague ill come upon them hen they are numbered.

Everyone tenty years of age or older ho crosses over must give this offering to the LORD.
In making the offering to the LORD to atone for your lives, the rich shall not give more than a half shekel, nor shall the poor give less.
Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. It ill serve as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD to make atonement for your lives.” \b
And the LORD said to Moses,
“ You are to make a bronze basin ith a bronze stand for ashing. Set it beteen the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put ater in it,
ith hich Aaron and his sons are to ash their hands and feet.
Whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister by presenting an offering made by fire to the LORD, they must ash ith ater so that they ill not die.
Thus they are to ash their hands and feet so that they ill not die; this shall be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.” \b
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Take the finest spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half that amount (250 shekels) of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
500 shekels of cassia —all according to the sanctuary shekel— and a hin of olive oil.
Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the ork of a perfumer; it ill be a sacred anointing oil. \b
Use this oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin ith its stand.
You are to consecrate them so that they ill be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests. \b
And you are to tell the Israelites, ’ This ill be My sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.
It must not be used to anoint an ordinary man, and you must not make anything like it ith the same formula. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
Anyone ho mixes perfume like it or puts it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’” \b
The LORD also said to Moses, “ Take fragrant spices— gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense— in equal measures,
and make a fragrant blend of incense, the ork of a perfumer, seasoned ith salt, pure and holy.
Grind some of it into fine poder and place it in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, here I ill meet ith you. It shall be most holy to you.
You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.
Anyone ho makes something like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.”
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him ith the Spirit of God, ith skill, ability, and knoledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
to design artistic orks in gold, silver, and bronze,
to cut gemstones for settings, and to carve ood, so that he may be a master of every craft. \b
Moreover, I have selected Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, as his assistant. \b
the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat upon it, and all the other furnishings of the tent—
the table ith its utensils, the pure gold lampstand ith all its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering ith all its utensils, and the basin ith its stand—
as ell as the oven garments, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests,
in addition to the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They are to make them according to all that I have commanded you.” \b
And the LORD said to Moses,
“ Tell the Israelites, ’ Surely you must keep My Sabbaths, for this ill be a sign beteen Me and you for the generations to come, so that you may kno that I am the LORD ho sanctifies you.
Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Anyone ho profanes it must surely be put to death. Whoever does any ork on that day must be cut off from among his people.
For six days ork may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any ork on the Sabbath day must surely be put to death. \b
The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, celebrating it as a permanent covenant for the generations to come.
It is a sign beteen Me and the Israelites forever; for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and as refreshed.’” \b
When the LORD had finished speaking ith Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the to tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.

Then the LORD said to Moses, “ Go don at once, for your people, hom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “ O LORD, hy does Your anger burn against Your people, hom You brought out of the land of Egypt ith great poer and a mighty hand?

Then Moses turned and ent don the mountain ith the to tablets of the Testimony in his hands. They ere inscribed on both sides, front and back.
The tablets ere the ork of God, and the riting as the riting of God, engraved on the tablets. \b
When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “ The sound of ar is in the camp.” \b
But Moses replied: \b “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!” \b
As Moses approached the camp and sa the calf and the dancing, he burned ith anger and thre the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.
Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to poder, and scattered the poder over the face of the ater. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it. \b

So I said to them, ’ Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And hen I thre it into the fire, out came this calf!” \b
Moses sa that the people ere out of control, for Aaron had let them run ild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “ Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” \b \b

Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and ash them ith ater.
And you are to clothe Aaron ith the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as a priest.
Bring his sons forard and clothe them ith tunics.
Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may also serve Me as priests. Their anointing ill qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.” \b
Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
So the tabernacle as set up on the first day of the first month of the second year. \b
When Moses set up the tabernacle, he laid its bases, positioned its frames, inserted its crossbars, and set up its posts.
Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, just as the LORD had commanded him. \b
Moses took the Testimony and placed it in the ark, attaching the poles to the ark; and he set the mercy seat atop the ark.
Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the veil for the screen, and shielded off the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded him. \b
Moses placed the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him. \b
He also placed the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle
and set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him. \b
Moses placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting, in front of the veil,
and he burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded him.
Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
He placed the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded him. \b
He placed the basin beteen the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put ater in it for ashing;
and from it Moses, Aaron, and his sons ashed their hands and feet.
They ashed henever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses. \b
And Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and he hung the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the ork. \b
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses as unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. \b
Whenever the cloud as lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites ould set out through all the stages of their journey.

For the cloud of the LORD as over the tabernacle by day, and fire as in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.
Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
“ Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you may bring as your offering an animal from the herd or the flock. \b
If one’s offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to present an unblemished male. He must bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for its acceptance before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him. \b
And he shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to present the blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Next, he is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces. \b
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put a fire on the altar and arrange ood on the fire.
Then Aaron’s sons the priests are to arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, atop the burning ood on the altar.
The entrails and legs must be ashed ith ater, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. \b
If, hoever, one’s offering is a burnt offering from the flock— from the sheep or goats— he is to present an unblemished male.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to sprinkle its blood against the altar on all sides.
He is to cut the animal into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and fat, atop the burning ood that is on the altar.
The entrails and legs must be ashed ith ater, and the priest shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. \b
If, instead, one’s offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to present a turtledove or a young pigeon.
Then the priest shall bring it to the altar, tist off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood should be drained out on the side of the altar.
And he is to remove the crop ith its contents and thro it to the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.

He shall tear it open by its ings, ithout dividing the bird completely. And the priest is to burn it on the altar atop the burning ood. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
“ When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must consist of fine flour. He is to pour olive oil on it, put frankincense on it,

and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together ith all the frankincense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. \b
No if you bring an offering of grain baked in an oven, it must consist of fine flour, either unleavened cakes mixed ith oil or unleavened afers coated ith oil. \b
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it must be unleavened bread made of fine flour mixed ith oil.
Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering. \b
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must consist of fine flour ith oil. \b
When you bring to the LORD the grain offering made in any of these ays, it is to be presented to the priest, and he shall take it to the altar.
The priest is to remove the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
But the remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. \b
No grain offering that you present to the LORD may be made ith leaven, for you are not to burn any leaven or honey as an offering made by fire to the LORD.

And you shall season each of your grain offerings ith salt. You must not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering; you are to add salt to each of your offerings. \b

“ If one’s offering is a peace offering and he offers an animal from the herd, hether male or female, he must present it ithout blemish before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar. \b
From the peace offering he is to bring an offering made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
both kidneys ith the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, hich he is to remove ith the kidneys.
Then Aaron’s sons are to burn it on the altar atop the burnt offering that is on the burning ood, as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. \b
If, hoever, one’s peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, he must present a male or female ithout blemish. \b
If he is presenting a lamb for his offering, he must present it before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar. \b

And from the peace offering he shall bring an offering made by fire to the LORD consisting of its fat: the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
both kidneys ith the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, hich he is to remove ith the kidneys.
Then the priest is to burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to the LORD. \b
If one’s offering is a goat, he is to present it before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar. \b
And from his offering he shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
both kidneys ith the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, hich he is to remove ith the kidneys.
Then the priest is to burn the food on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat is the LORD’s. \b
This is a permanent statute for the generations to come, herever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.”
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Tell the Israelites to do as follos ith one ho sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s commandments and does hat is forbidden by them: \b
If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull ithout blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.

Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest must then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. And he is to pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Then he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering— the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
both kidneys ith the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, hich he is to remove ith the kidneys—
just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering. Then the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, ith its head and legs and its entrails and dung—
all the rest of the bull— he must take outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place here the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a ood fire on the ash heap. \b

No if the hole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly so that they violate any of the LORD’s commandments and incur guilt by doing hat is forbidden,
hen they become aare of the sin they have committed, then the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
Then the anointed priest is to bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting,
and he is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the veil.

He is also to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and he must pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
And he is to remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar.
He shall offer this bull just as he did the bull for the sin offering; in this ay the priest ill make atonement on their behalf, and they ill be forgiven.
Then he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly. \b
When a leader sins unintentionally and does hat is prohibited by any of the commandments of the LORD his God, he incurs guilt.
When he becomes aare of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it at the place here the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering ith his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
He must burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offerings; thus the priest ill make atonement for that man’s sin, and he ill be forgiven. \b
And if one of the common people sins unintentionally and does hat is prohibited by any of the LORD’s commandments, he incurs guilt.
When he becomes aare of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished female goat as his offering for that sin.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
Then the priest is to take some of its blood ith his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

Then he is to remove all the fat, just as it is removed from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. In this ay the priest ill make atonement for him, and he ill be forgiven. \b
If, hoever, he brings a lamb as a sin offering, he must bring an unblemished female.
And he is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place here the burnt offering is slaughtered.
Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering ith his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

And he shall remove all the fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offerings, and he shall burn it on the altar along ith the offerings made by fire to the LORD. In this ay the priest ill make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he ill be forgiven.
“ If someone sins by failing to testify hen he hears a public charge about something he has itnessed, hether he has seen it or learned of it, he shall bear the iniquity. \b
Or if a person touches anything unclean— hether the carcass of any unclean ild animal or livestock or craling creature—even if he is unaare of it, he is unclean and guilty. \b
Or if he touches human uncleanness— anything by hich one becomes unclean— even if he is unaare of it, hen he realizes it, he is guilty. \b

Or if someone sears thoughtlessly ith his lips to do anything good or evil— in hatever matter a man may rashly pronounce an oath— even if he is unaare of it, hen he realizes it, he is guilty in the matter. \b
If someone incurs guilt in one of these ays, he must confess the sin he has committed,
and he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. And the priest ill make atonement for him concerning his sin. \b
If, hoever, he cannot afford a lamb, he may bring to the LORD as restitution for his sin to turtledoves or to young pigeons— one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.

He is to bring it to the priest, ho shall take a handful from it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar atop the offerings made by fire to the LORD; it is a sin offering.
In this ay the priest ill make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he ill be forgiven. The remainder ill belong to the priest, like the grain offering.” \b
Then the LORD said to Moses,

“ If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, of proper value in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.

Regarding any holy thing he has harmed, he must make restitution by adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest, ho ill make atonement on his behalf ith the ram as a guilt offering, and he ill be forgiven. \b
If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments even though he as unaare, he is guilty and shall bear his punishment.

He is to bring to the priest an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock as a guilt offering. Then the priest ill make atonement on his behalf for the rong he has committed in ignorance, and he ill be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering; he as certainly guilty before the LORD.”
And the LORD said to Moses,
“ If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in regard to a deposit or security entrusted to him or stolen, or if he extorts his neighbor
or finds lost property and lies about it and sears falsely, or if he commits any such sin that a man might commit—
once he has sinned and becomes guilty, he must return hat he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
or anything else about hich he has sorn falsely. \b
Then he must bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.
In this ay the priest ill make atonement for him before the LORD, and he ill be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.” \b
Then the LORD said to Moses,

“Command Aaron and his sons that this is the la of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar. \b
And the priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, and he shall remove from the altar the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside it.

The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not be extinguished. Every morning the priest is to add ood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.

No this is the la of the grain offering: Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.

The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil, together ith all the frankincense from the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. \b

Any male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. This is a permanent portion from the offerings made by fire to the LORD for the generations to come. Anything that touches them ill become holy.” \b
Then the LORD said to Moses,

“ This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
It shall be prepared ith oil on a griddle; you are to bring it ell-kneaded and present it as a grain offering broken in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

And the LORD said to Moses,
“Tell Aaron and his sons that this is the la of the sin offering: In the place here the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.
The priest ho offers it shall eat it; it must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Anything that touches its flesh ill become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must ash it in a holy place. \b
The clay pot in hich the sin offering is boiled must be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scoured and rinsed ith ater.
Any male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned.
“No this is the la of the guilt offering, hich is most holy:
The guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place here the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest shall sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.
And all the fat from it shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
both kidneys ith the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, hich is to be removed ith the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat of it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy. \b
The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same la applies to both. It belongs to the priest ho makes atonement ith it.
As for the priest ho presents a burnt offering for anyone, the hide of that offering belongs to him.
Likeise, every grain offering that is baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest ho presents it,
and every grain offering, hether dry or mixed ith oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron. \b
No this is the la of the peace offering that one may present to the LORD:

If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along ith the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed ith olive oil, unleavened afers coated ith oil, and ell-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed ith oil. \b
Along ith his peace offering of thanksgiving he is to present an offering ith cakes of leavened bread.
From the cakes he must present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest ho sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning. \b
If, hoever, the sacrifice he offers is a vo or a freeill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but the remainder may be eaten on the next day.
But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.

If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it ill not be accepted. It ill not be credited to the one ho presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one ho eats of it shall bear his iniquity. \b
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it is to be burned up. As for any other meat, anyone ho is ceremonially clean may eat it.
But if anyone ho is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.

If one touches anything unclean, hether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing, and then eats any of the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.” \b
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to the Israelites and say, ’ You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
The fat of an animal found dead or mauled by ild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it. \b
If anyone eats the fat of an animal from hich an offering made by fire may be presented to the LORD, the one ho eats it must be cut off from his people.

Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to the Israelites and say, ’Anyone ho presents a peace offering to the LORD must bring it as his sacrifice to the LORD.
With his on hands he is to bring the offerings made by fire to the LORD; he shall bring the fat, together ith the breast, and ave the breast as a ave offering before the LORD. \b
The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offering.
The son of Aaron ho presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion. \b

This is the portion of the offerings made by fire to the LORD for Aaron and his sons since the day they ere presented to serve the LORD as priests.
On the day they ere anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the sons of Israel. It is a permanent portion for the generations to come. \b
This is the la of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
hich the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Take Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the to rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
and assemble the hole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” \b
So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
And Moses said to them, “ This is hat the LORD has commanded to be done.” \b
