Moses slaughtered the bull, took some of the blood, and applied it ith his finger to all four horns of the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it. \b

Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Moses also presented Aaron’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he sprinkled the blood on all sides of the altar. \b
And Moses took the fat— the fat tail, all the fat that as on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys ith their fat— as ell as the right thigh.

And from the basket of unleavened bread that as before the LORD, he took one cake of unleavened bread, one cake of bread made ith oil, and one afer, and he placed them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and aved them before the LORD as a ave offering. \b
Then Moses took these from their hands and burned them on the altar ith the burnt offering. This as an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
He also took the breast— Moses’ portion of the ram of ordination— and aved it before the LORD as a ave offering, as the LORD had commanded him. \b

Next, Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that as on the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, as ell as Aaron’s sons and their garments. \b

And Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “ Boil the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and eat it there ith the bread that is in the basket of ordination offerings, as I commanded, saying, ’Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’
Then you must burn up the remainder of the meat and bread. \b
You must not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are complete; for it ill take seven days to ordain you.
What has been done today has been commanded by the LORD in order to make atonement on your behalf.

This is to be a permanent statute for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any ork—hether the native or the foreigner ho resides among you—

The priest ho is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest shall make atonement. He ill put on the sacred linen garments
and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.

Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites and tell them this is hat the LORD has commanded:
’Anyone from the house of Israel ho slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside of it

instead of bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before His tabernacle— that man shall incur bloodguilt. He has shed blood and must be cut off from among his people. \b

If anyone from the house of Israel or a foreigner living among them eats any blood, I ill set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.

Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God.

You must not follo the practices of the land of Egypt, here you used to live, and you must not follo the practices of the land of Canaan, into hich I am bringing you. You must not alk in their customs. \b

But you are to keep My statutes and ordinances, and you must not commit any of these abominations— neither your native-born nor the foreigner ho lives among you.

You must keep My charge not to practice any of the abominable customs that ere practiced before you, so that you do not defile yourselves by them. I am the LORD your God.”
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“ Speak to the hole congregation of Israel and tell them: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy. \b
Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must keep My Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God. \b
Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods. I am the LORD your God. \b
When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it for your acceptance.

When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.

You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another. \b
You must not sear falsely by My name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD. \b
You must not defraud your neighbor or rob him. \b \b
You must not curse the deaf or place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD. \b
You must not pervert justice; you must not sho partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly. \b
You must not go about spreading slander among your people. \b \b
You must not harbor hatred against your brother in your heart. Directly rebuke your neighbor, so that you ill not incur guilt on account of him.
Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD. \b

You are to keep My statutes. You shall not crossbreed to different kinds of livestock; you shall not so your fields ith to kinds of seed; and you shall not ear clothing made of to kinds of material. \b

If a man lies carnally ith a slave girl promised to another man but ho has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. But they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
The man, hoever, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD.

Then the LORD said to Moses,

Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and tell them that a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people,

When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, ho defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city as Avith. \b \li1
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place. \b \li1
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigned in his place. \b \li1
When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place. \b \li1
When Baal-hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place. His city as named Pau, and his ife’s name as Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab. \b \li1
Then Hadad died. \b
Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
Magdiel, and Iram. These ere the chiefs of Edom.
These ere the sons of Israel: \b \li1 Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. \b \li1
The sons of Judah: \b \li2 Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three ere born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah’s firstborn, as icked in the sight of the LORD, ho put him to death. \b \li2
Tamar, Judah’s daughter-in-la, bore to him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all. \b \li1
The sons of Perez: \b \li2 Hezron and Hamul. \b \li1
The sons of Zerah: \b \li2 Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara —five in all. \b \li1
The son of Carmi: \b \li2 Achar, ho brought trouble upon Israel by violating the ban on devoted things. \b \li1
The son of Ethan: \b \li2 Azariah. \b \li1
The sons ho ere born to Hezron: \b \li2 Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb. \b \li1
Ram as the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab as the father of Nahshon, a leader of the descendants of Judah. \b \li1
Nahshon as the father of Salmon, and Salmon as the father of Boaz. \b \li1
Boaz as the father of Obed, and Obed as the father of Jesse. \b \li1
Jesse as the father of Eliab his firstborn; Abinadab as born second, Shimea third,
Nethanel fourth, Raddai fifth,
Ozem sixth, and David seventh.
Their sisters ere Zeruiah and Abigail. And the three sons of Zeruiah ere Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail as the mother of Amasa, hose father as Jether the Ishmaelite. \b \li1
Caleb son of Hezron had children by his ife Azubah and by Jerioth. These ere the sons of Azubah: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, ho bore to him Hur.
Hur as the father of Uri, and Uri as the father of Bezalel. \b \li1
Later, Hezron slept ith the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead. He had married her hen he as sixty years old, and she bore to him Segub.
Segub as the father of Jair, ho had tenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram captured Havvoth-jair, along ith Kenath and its sixty surrounding villages. All these ere descendants of Machir the father of Gilead. \b \li1
After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his ife Abijah bore to him Ashhur the father of Tekoa. \b \li1
The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron: \b \li2 Ram his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another ife named Atarah, ho as the mother of Onam. \b \li1
The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel: \b \li2 Maaz, Jamin, and Eker. \b \li1
The sons of Onam: \b \li2 Shammai and Jada. \b \li1 The sons of Shammai: \b \li2 Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur’s ife as named Abihail, and she bore to him Ahban and Molid. \b \li1
The sons of Nadab: \b \li2 Seled and Appaim. Seled died ithout children. \b \li1
The son of Appaim: \b \li2 Ishi. \b \li1 The son of Ishi: \b \li2 Sheshan. \b \li1 The son of Sheshan: \b \li2 Ahlai. \b \li1
The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: \b \li2 Jether and Jonathan. Jether died ithout children. \b \li1
The sons of Jonathan: \b \li2 Peleth and Zaza. \b \li1 These ere the descendants of Jerahmeel. \b \li1
Sheshan had no sons, but only daughters; but he did have an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore to him Attai. \b \li1
Attai as the father of Nathan, Nathan as the father of Zabad,
Zabad as the father of Ephlal, Ephlal as the father of Obed,
Obed as the father of Jehu, Jehu as the father of Azariah,
Azariah as the father of Helez, Helez as the father of Elasah,
Elasah as the father of Sismai, Sismai as the father of Shallum,
Shallum as the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah as the father of Elishama. \b \li1
The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: \b \li2 Mesha his firstborn, ho as the father of Ziph, and Mareshah his second son, ho as the father of Hebron. \b \li1
The sons of Hebron: \b \li2 Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema as the father of Raham the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem as the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai as Maon, and Maon as the father of Beth-zur. \b \li1
Caleb’s concubine Ephah as the mother of Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran as the father of Gazez. \b \li1
The sons of Jahdai: \b \li2 Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph. \b \li1
Caleb’s concubine Maacah as the mother of Sheber and Tirhanah.
She as also the mother of Shaaph father of Madmannah, and of Sheva father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb’s daughter as Acsah.
These ere the descendants of Caleb. \b \li1 The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: \b \li2 Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader. \b \li1
These ere the descendants of Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim: \b \li2 Haroeh, half the Manahathites,
and the clans of Kiriath-jearim—the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From these descended the Zorathites and Eshtaolites. \b \li1
The descendants of Salma: \b \li2 Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half the Manahathites, the Zorites,
and the clans of the scribes ho lived at Jabez—the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These are the Kenites ho came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
These ere the sons of David ho ere born to him in Hebron: \b \li1 The firstborn as Amnon by Ahinoam of Jezreel; \b \li1 the second as Daniel by Abigail of Carmel; \b \li1
the third as Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur; \b \li1 the fourth as Adonijah the son of Haggith; \b \li1
the fifth as Shephatiah by Abital; \b \li1 and the sixth as Ithream by his ife Eglah. \b \li1
These six sons ere born to David in Hebron, here he reigned seven years and six months. \b
and these sons ere born to him in Jerusalem: \b \li1 Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. These four ere born to him by Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel. \b \li1
David’s other sons ere Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet—nine in all. \b \li1
These ere all the sons of David, besides the sons by his concubines. And Tamar as their sister. \b \li1
Solomon’s son as Rehoboam: \b \li2 Abijah as his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, and Josiah his son. \b \li1
The sons of Josiah: \b \li2 Johanan as the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth. \b \li1
The successors of Jehoiakim: \b \li2 Jeconiah his son, and Zedekiah. \b \li1
The descendants of Jeconiah the captive: \b \li2 Shealtiel his son,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. \b \li1
The sons of Pedaiah: \b \li2 Zerubbabel and Shimei. \b \li1 The children of Zerubbabel: \b \li2 Meshullam and Hananiah, their sister Shelomith,
and five others: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed. \b \li1
The descendants of Hananiah: \b \li2 Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, and the sons of Rephaiah, of Arnan, of Obadiah, and of Shecaniah. \b \li1
The six descendants of Shecaniah ere Shemaiah and his sons: \b \li2 Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat. \b \li1
The sons of Neariah: \b \li2 Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam—three in all. \b \li1
The sons of Elioenai: \b \li2 Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven in all.
The descendants of Judah: \b \li1 Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal. \b \li1
Reaiah son of Shobal as the father of Jahath, and Jahath as the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These ere the clans of the Zorathites. \b \li1
These ere the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. And their sister as named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel as the father of Gedor, and Ezer as the father of Hushah. \b \li1 These ere the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah and the father of Bethlehem. \b \li1
Ashhur the father of Tekoa had to ives, Helah and Naarah. \b \li2
Naarah bore to him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These ere the descendants of Naarah. \b \li2
The sons of Helah ere Zereth, Zohar, Ethnan,
and Koz, ho as the father of Anub and Zobebah and of the clans of Aharhel son of Harum. \b \li1
No Jabez as more honorable than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez, saying, “Because I bore him in pain.” \b \li1

And Jabez called out to the God of Israel, “If only You ould bless me and enlarge my territory! May Your hand be ith me and keep me from harm, so that I ill be free from pain.” \b \li1 And God granted the request of Jabez. \b \li1
Chelub the brother of Shuhah as the father of Mehir, ho as the father of Eshton.
Eshton as the father of Beth-rapha, of Paseah, and of Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These ere the men of Recah. \b \li1
The sons of Kenaz: \b \li2 Othniel and Seraiah. \b \li1 The sons of Othniel: \b \li2 Hathath and Meonothai. \b \li1
Meonothai as the father of Ophrah, and Seraiah as the father of Joab, the father of those living in Ge-harashim, hich as given this name because its people ere craftsmen. \b \li1
The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: \b \li2 Iru, Elah, and Naam. \b \li1 The son of Elah: \b \li2 Kenaz. \b \li1
The sons of Jehallelel: \b \li2 Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel. \b \li1
The sons of Ezrah: \b \li2 Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. \b \li2 And Mered’s ife Bithiah gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.

These ere the children of Pharaoh’s daughter Bithiah. \b \li2 Mered also took a Judean ife, ho gave birth to Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. \b \li1
The sons of Hodiah’s ife, the sister of Naham, ere the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and of Eshtemoa the Maacathite. \b \li1
The sons of Shimon: \b \li2 Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. \b \li1 The descendants of Ishi: \b \li2 Zoheth and Ben-zoheth. \b \li1
The sons of Shelah son of Judah: \b \li2 Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah and the clans of the linen orkers at Beth-ashbea,
Jokim, the men of Cozeba, and Joash and Saraph, ho ruled in Moab and Jashubi-lehem. (These names are from ancient records.)
These ere the potters ho lived at Netaim and Gederah. They lived there in the service of the king. \b
The descendants of Simeon: \b \li1 Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. \b \li1
The sons of Shaul: \b \li2 Shallum, Mibsam, and Mishma. \b \li1
The sons of Mishma: \b \li2 Hammuel, Zaccur, and Shimei. \b \li1
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children, so their hole clan did not become as numerous as the sons of Judah.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These ere their cities until the reign of David.
And their villages ere Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five tons—
and all their surrounding villages as far as Baal. These ere their settlements, and they kept a genealogical record: \b \li2
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah (son of Seraiah, son of Asiel),
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi (son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah). \b \li1
These men listed by name ere the leaders of their clans. Their families increased greatly,
and they journeyed to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, in search of pasture for their flocks.
There they found rich, good pasture, and the land as spacious, peaceful, and quiet; for some Hamites had lived there formerly. \b \li1

These ho ere noted by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites and Meunites there in their dellings, devoting them to destruction even to this day. Then they settled in their place, because there as pasture for their flocks.
And five hundred of these Simeonites led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, ent to Mount Seir
and struck don the remnant of the Amalekites ho had escaped. And they have lived there to this day.

These ere the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel. Though he as the firstborn, his birthright as given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, because Reuben defiled his father’s bed. So he is not reckoned according to birthright.
And though Judah prevailed over his brothers and a ruler came from him, the birthright belonged to Joseph.
The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: \b Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. \b \li1
The descendants of Joel: \b \li2 Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
and Beerah his son, hom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried into exile. \b \li1 Beerah as a leader of the Reubenites.
His relatives by their clans are recorded in their genealogy: \b \li2 Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. They settled in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
They also settled in the east as far as the edge of the desert that extends to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead. \b \li2
During the days of Saul they aged ar against the Hagrites, ho ere defeated at their hands, and they occupied the homes of the Hagrites throughout the region east of Gilead. \b
The descendants of Gad lived next to the Reubenites in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah: \b \li1
Joel as the chief, Shapham the second, then Jaanai and Shaphat, ho lived in Bashan. \b \li1
Their kinsmen by families ere Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.
These ere the sons of Abihail son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, as head of their family. \b \li1
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its tons, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon.
All of them ere reckoned in the genealogies during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel. \b \li1
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 arriors—valiant men ho carried the shield and sord, dre the bo, and ere trained for battle.
They aged ar against the Hagrites, as ell as Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab. \b \li1

And because they cried out to God in battle, they ere helped against their enemies, and the Hagrites and all their allies ere delivered into their hands. Because they put their trust in God, He ansered their prayers.
They seized the livestock of the Hagrites—50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 captives,
and many others fell slain, because the battle belonged to God. And they occupied the land until the exile. \b
No the people of the half-tribe of Manasseh ere numerous. They settled in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon ( that is, Senir, also knon as Mount Hermon).
These ere the heads of their families: \b \li1 Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. \b \li1 They ere mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their families.
But they ere unfaithful to the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves ith the gods of the peoples of the land, hom God had destroyed before them. \b \li1

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria) to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. And he brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, here they remain to this day.
The sons of Levi: \b \li1 Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. \b \li1
The sons of Kohath: \b \li2 Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. \b \li1
The children of Amram: \b \li2 Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. \b \li1 The sons of Aaron: \b \li2 Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. \b \li2
Eleazar as the father of Phinehas, \b \li2 Phinehas as the father of Abishua, \b \li2
Abishua as the father of Bukki, \b \li2 Bukki as the father of Uzzi, \b \li2
Uzzi as the father of Zerahiah, \b \li2 Zerahiah as the father of Meraioth, \b \li2
Meraioth as the father of Amariah, \b \li2 Amariah as the father of Ahitub, \b \li2
Ahitub as the father of Zadok, \b \li2 Zadok as the father of Ahimaaz, \b \li2
Ahimaaz as the father of Azariah, \b \li2 Azariah as the father of Johanan, \b \li2
Johanan as the father of Azariah, ho served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem, \b \li2
Azariah as the father of Amariah, \b \li2 Amariah as the father of Ahitub, \b \li2
Ahitub as the father of Zadok, \b \li2 Zadok as the father of Shallum, \b \li2
Shallum as the father of Hilkiah, \b \li2 Hilkiah as the father of Azariah, \b \li2
Azariah as the father of Seraiah, \b \li2 and Seraiah as the father of Jehozadak. \b \li1
Jehozadak ent into captivity hen the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. \b
The sons of Levi: \b \li1 Gershom, Kohath, and Merari. \b \li1
These are the names of the sons of Gershom: \b \li2 Libni and Shimei. \b \li1
The sons of Kohath: \b \li2 Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. \b \li1
The sons of Merari: \b \li2 Mahli and Mushi. \b \b \li1
Of Gershom: \b \li2 Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeatherai his son. \b \li1
The descendants of Kohath: \b \li2 Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son. \b \li1
The descendants of Elkanah: \b \li2 Amasai, Ahimoth,
Elkanah his son, Zophai his son, Nahath his son,
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, and Elkanah his son. \b \li1
The sons of Samuel: \b \li2 Joel his firstborn and Abijah his second son. \b \li1
The descendants of Merari: \b \li2 Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, and Asaiah his son. \b
These are the men David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD after the ark rested there.
They ministered ith song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. And they performed their duties according to the regulations given them.
These are the men ho served, together ith their sons. \b \li1 From the Kohathites: \b \li2 Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel. \b \li1
Heman’s kinsman as Asaph, ho served at his right hand: \b \li2 Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi. \b \li1
On the left ere their kinsmen, the sons of Merari: \b \li2 Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi. \b
Their fello Levites ere assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God.

But Aaron and his sons did all the ork of the Most Holy Place. They presented the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded. \b \li1
These ere the descendants of Aaron: \b \li2 Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son. \b
No these ere the territories assigned to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clan for their settlements, because the first lot fell to them: \b \li1
They ere given Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands.
But the fields and villages around the city ere given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
So the descendants of Aaron ere given Hebron (a city of refuge), Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa,
Hilen, Debir,
Ashan, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
And from the tribe of Benjamin they ere given Gibeon, Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, together ith their pasturelands. So they had thirteen cities in all among their families. \b \li1
To the rest of the Kohathites, ten cities ere allotted from the half-tribe of Manasseh. \b
The Gershomites , according to their clans, ere allotted thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan. \b
The Merarites, according to their families, ere allotted telve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. \b
So the Israelites gave to the Levites these cities and their pasturelands.
They assigned by lot the cities named above from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. \b
And some of the clans of the Kohathites ere given cities from the tribe of Ephraim for their territory: \b \li1
They ere given Shechem (a city of refuge) ith its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer,
Jokmeam, Beth-horon,
Aijalon, and Gath-rimmon, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh the remaining clans of the Kohathites ere given Aner and Bileam, together ith their pasturelands. \b
The Gershomites received the folloing: \b \li1 From the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh they ere given Golan in Bashan and also Ashtaroth, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
From the tribe of Issachar they ere given Kedesh, Daberath,
Ramoth, and Anem, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
From the tribe of Asher they ere given Mashal, Abdon,
Hukok, and Rehob, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
And from the tribe of Naphtali they ere given Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, together ith their pasturelands. \b
The Merarites (the rest of the Levites) received the folloing: \b \li1 From the tribe of Zebulun they ere given Rimmono and Tabor, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
From the tribe of Reuben east of the Jordan opposite Jericho they ere given Bezer in the ilderness, Jahzah,
Kedemoth, and Mephaath, together ith their pasturelands. \b \li1
And from the tribe of Gad they ere given Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,

Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: \b

Then Job ansered: \b

“ My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave aaits me.

Then Bildad the Shuhite replied: \b

Then Job ansered: \b

Then Zophar the Naamathite replied: \b

Then Job ansered: \b

Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: \b

Then Job ansered: \b

“ Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those ho kno Him never see His days?

Then Job ansered: \b

Job continued his discourse: \b

And Job continued his discourse: \b
“ Ho I long for the months gone by, for the days hen God atched over me,

I sa something else under the sun: The race is not to the sift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the ise, nor the ealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.

I have also seen this isdom under the sun, and it as great to me:

before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,

This is Solomon’s Song of Songs. \b

You ill keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.
For He has humbled those ho dell on high; He lays the lofty city lo. He brings it don to the ground; He casts it into the dust.
Feet trample it don— the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor. \b
The path of the righteous is level; You clear a straight path for the upright.
Yes, e ait for You, O LORD; e alk in the path of Your judgments. Your name and renon are the desire of our souls.
My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dan. For hen Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the orld learn righteousness.
Though grace is shon to the icked man, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of righteousness he acts unjustly and fails to see the majesty of the LORD. \b
O LORD, Your hand is upraised, but they do not see it. They ill see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. The fire set for Your enemies ill consume them!
O LORD, You ill establish peace for us. For all that e have accomplished, You have done for us.
O LORD our God, other lords besides You have had dominion, but Your name alone do e confess. \b
The dead ill not live; the departed spirits ill not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have iped out all memory of them.
You have enlarged the nation, O LORD; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land. \b
O LORD, they sought You in their distress; hen You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
As a oman ith child about to give birth rithes and cries out in pain, so ere e in Your presence, O LORD.
We ere ith child; e rithed in pain; but e gave birth to ind. We have given no salvation to the earth, nor brought any life into the orld. \b
Your dead ill live; their bodies ill rise. Aake and sing, you ho dell in the dust! For your de is like the de of the morning, and the earth ill bring forth her dead. \b
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little hile until the rath has passed.
For behold, the LORD is coming out of His delling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth ill reveal her bloodshed and ill no longer conceal her slain.
In that day the LORD ill take His sharp, great, and mighty sord, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent — Leviathan the coiling serpent— and He ill slay the dragon of the sea.
In that day: \b “ Sing about a fruitful vineyard.
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I ater it continually. I guard it night and day so no one can disturb it;
I am not angry. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I ould march and trample them, I ould burn them to the ground.
Or let them lay claim to My protection; let them make peace ith Me— yes, let them make peace ith Me.” \b
In the days to come, Jacob ill take root. Israel ill bud and blossom and fill the hole orld ith fruit. \b
Has the LORD struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those ho slayed her?
By arfare and exile You contended ith her and removed her ith a fierce ind, as on the day the east ind blos.

Therefore Jacob’s guilt ill be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin ill be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars ill remain standing. \b
For the fortified city lies deserted— a homestead abandoned, a ilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie don; they strip its branches bare.

When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people ithout understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shos them no favor. \b
In that day the LORD ill thresh from the floing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, ill be gathered one by one.

Woe to the majestic cron of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading floer of his glorious splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, the pride of those overcome by ine.
Behold, the Lord has one ho is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest, like a driving rain or flooding donpour, he ill smash that cron to the ground.

On that day the LORD of Hosts ill be a cron of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people,
a spirit of justice to him ho sits in judgment, and a strength to those ho repel the onslaught at the gate. \b

These also stagger from ine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by ine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.

to hom He has said: “ This is the place of rest, let the eary rest; this is the place of repose.” \b But they ould not listen. \b

For you said, “ We have made a covenant ith death; e have fashioned an agreement ith Sheol. When the overhelming scourge passes through it ill not touch us, because e have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.” \b
So this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b “ See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one ho believes ill never be shaken.
I ill make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail ill seep aay your refuge of lies, and ater ill flood your hiding place.
Your covenant ith death ill be dissolved, and your agreement ith Sheol ill not stand. When the overhelming scourge passes through, you ill be trampled by it.
As often as it passes through, it ill carry you aay; it ill seep through morning after morning, by day and by night.” \b The understanding of this message ill bring sheer terror.
Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to rap around you.
For the LORD ill rise up as at Mount Perazim. He ill rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His ork, His strange ork, and to perform His task, His disturbing task. \b
So no, do not mock, or your shackles ill become heavier. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the hole land. \b
Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear hat I say.
Does the ploman plo for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harro the soil?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not so caraay and scatter cumin? He plants heat in ros and barley in plots, and rye ithin its border. \b
For his God instructs and teaches him properly.
Surely caraay is not threshed ith a sledge, and the heel of a cart is not rolled over the cumin. But caraay is beaten out ith a stick, and cumin ith a rod.
Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed. Though the heels of the cart roll over it, the horses do not crush it.
This also comes from the LORD of Hosts, ho is onderful in counsel and excellent in isdom.
Woe to you, O Ariel, the city of Ariel here David camped! Year upon year let your festivals recur.
And I ill constrain Ariel, and there ill be mourning and lamentation; she ill be like an altar hearth before Me.
I ill camp in a circle around you; I ill besiege you ith toers and set up siege orks against you.
You ill be brought lo, you ill speak from the ground, and out of the dust your ords ill be muffled. Your voice ill be like a spirit from the ground; your speech ill hisper out of the dust. \b
But your many foes ill be like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like bloing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
you ill be visited by the LORD of Hosts ith thunder and earthquake and loud noise, ith indstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire.
All the many nations going out to battle against Ariel— even all ho ar against her, laying siege and attacking her— ill be like a dream, like a vision in the night,

as hen a hungry man dreams he is eating, then aakens still hungry; as hen a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, then aakens faint and parched. So ill it be for all the many nations ho go to battle against Mount Zion. \b
Stop and be astonished; blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not ith ine; stagger, but not from strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers. \b
And the entire vision ill be to you like the ords sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone to read, he ill say, “ I cannot, because it is sealed.”
Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read, he ill say, “ I cannot read.” \b
Therefore the Lord said: \b “ These people dra near to Me ith their mouths and honor Me ith their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their orship of Me is but rules taught by men.
Therefore I ill again confound these people ith onder upon onder. The isdom of the ise ill vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent ill be hidden.” \b
Woe to those ho dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD. In darkness they do their orks and say, “ Who sees us, and ho ill kno?”

You have turned things upside don, as if the potter ere regarded as clay. Shall hat is formed say to him ho formed it, “ He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “ He has no understanding”? \b
In a very short time, ill not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?
On that day the deaf ill hear the ords of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind ill see.
The humble ill increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men ill rejoice in the Holy One of Israel. \b
For the ruthless ill vanish, the mockers ill disappear, and all ho look for evil ill be cut don—
those ho indict a man ith a ord, ho ensnare the mediator at the gate, and ho ith false charges deprive the innocent of justice. \b
Therefore the LORD ho redeemed Abraham says of the house of Jacob: \b “ No longer ill Jacob be ashamed and no more ill his face gro pale.

“ Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD, “ to those ho carry out a plan that is not Mine, ho form an alliance, but against My ill, heaping up sin upon sin.

This is the burden against the beasts of the Negev: \b Through a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their ealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people of no profit to them.

Then He ill send rain for the seed that you have son in the ground, and the food that comes from your land ill be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle ill graze in open pastures.

And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of ater ill flo in the day of great slaughter, hen the toers fall.

The light of the moon ill be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun ill be seven times brighter— like the light of seven days— on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the ounds He has inflicted. \b

You ill sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart ill rejoice like one ho alks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
And the LORD ill cause His majestic voice to be heard and His mighty arm to be revealed, striking in angry rath ith a flame of consuming fire, and ith cloudburst, storm, and hailstones. \b
For Assyria ill be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He ill strike them ith His scepter.
And ith every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings don on them, the tambourines and lyres ill sound as He battles ith eapons brandished.

For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and ide, ith plenty of fire and ood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.

Woe to those ho go don to Egypt for help, ho rely on horses, ho trust in their abundance of chariots and in their multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.

For this is hat the LORD has said to me: \b “ Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey— and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor— so the LORD of Hosts ill come don to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts ill protect Jerusalem. He ill shield it and deliver it; He ill pass over it and preserve it.” \b
Return to the One against hom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel.
For on that day, every one of you ill reject the idols of silver and gold that your on hands have sinfully made. \b
“ Then Assyria ill fall, but not by the sord of man; a sord ill devour them, but not one made by mortals. They ill flee before the sord, and their young men ill be put to forced labor.
Their rock ill pass aay for fear, and their princes ill panic at the sight of the battle standard,” declares the LORD, hose fire is in Zion, hose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Behold, a king ill reign in righteousness, and princes ill rule ith justice.
Each ill be like a shelter from the ind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of ater in a dry land, like the shado of a great rock in an arid land.
Then the eyes of those ho see ill no longer be closed, and the ears of those ho hear ill listen.

No longer ill a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.
For a fool speaks foolishness; his mind plots iniquity. He practices ungodliness and speaks falsely about the LORD; he leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink.
The eapons of the scoundrel are destructive; he hatches plots to destroy the poor ith lies, even hen the plea of the needy is just.
But a noble man makes honorable plans; he stands up for orthy causes. \b
Stand up, you complacent omen; listen to me. Give ear to my ord, you overconfident daughters.
In a little more than a year you ill tremble, O secure ones. For the grape harvest ill fail and the fruit harvest ill not arrive. \b
Shudder, you ladies of leisure; tremble, you daughters of complacency. Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth around your aists.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines,
and for the land of my people, overgron ith thorns and briers— even for every house of merriment in this city of revelry. \b
For the palace ill be forsaken, the busy city abandoned. The hill and the atchtoer ill become caves forever— the delight of ild donkeys and a pasture for flocks—
until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. \b Then the desert ill be an orchard, and the orchard ill seem like a forest.
Then justice ill inhabit the ilderness, and righteousness ill dell in the fertile field.
The ork of righteousness ill be peace; the service of righteousness ill be quiet confidence forever. \b
Then my people ill dell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
But hail ill level the forest, and the city ill sink to the depths. \b
Blessed are those ho so beside abundant aters, ho let the ox and donkey range freely.
Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you ill be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you ill be betrayed. \b
O LORD, be gracious to us! We ait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter hen You rise.
Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a sarm of locusts men seep over it. \b
The LORD is exalted, for He dells on high; He has filled Zion ith justice and righteousness.
He ill be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, isdom, and knoledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure. \b
Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace eep bitterly.
The highays are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the itnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves. \b
“ No I ill arise,” says the LORD. “ No I ill lift Myself up. No I ill be exalted.
You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that ill consume you.
The peoples ill be burned to ashes, like thorns cut don and set ablaze.
You ho are far off, hear hat I have done; you ho are near, acknoledge My might.” \b
The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “ Who of us can dell ith a consuming fire? Who of us can dell ith everlasting flames?”
He ho alks righteously and speaks ith sincerity, ho refuses gain from extortion, hose hand never takes a bribe, ho stops his ears against murderous plots and shuts his eyes tightly against evil—
he ill dell on the heights; the mountain fortress ill be his refuge; his food ill be provided and his ater assured. \b
Your eyes ill see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
Your mind ill ponder the former terror: “Where is he ho tallies? Where is he ho eighs? Where is he ho counts the toers?”
You ill no longer see the insolent, a people hose speech is unintelligible, ho stammer in a language you cannot understand. \b
Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes ill see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not ander; its tent pegs ill not be pulled up, nor ill any of its cords be broken.
But there the Majestic One, our LORD, ill be for us a place of rivers and ide canals, here no galley ith oars ill ro, and no majestic vessel ill pass. \b
For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lagiver, the LORD is our King. It is He ho ill save us. \b
Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils ill be divided, and even the lame ill carry off plunder.
And no resident of Zion ill say, “ I am sick.” The people ho dell there ill be forgiven of iniquity.
Come near, O nations, to listen; pay attention, O peoples. Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the orld and all that springs from it.
The LORD is angry ith all the nations and furious ith all their armies. He ill devote them to destruction; He ill give them over to slaughter.
Their slain ill be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses ill rise; the mountains ill flo ith their blood.
All the stars of heaven ill be dissolved. The skies ill be rolled up like a scroll, and all their stars ill fall like ithered leaves from the vine, like foliage from the fig tree. \b
When My sord has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it ill come don upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.

The sord of the LORD is bathed in blood. It drips ith fat— ith the blood of lambs and goats, ith the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

It ill not be quenched— day or night. Its smoke ill ascend forever. From generation to generation it ill lie desolate; no one ill ever again pass through it.
The desert ol and screech ol ill possess it, and the great ol and raven ill dell in it. \b The LORD ill stretch out over Edom a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.
No nobles ill be left to proclaim a king, and all her princes ill come to nothing.
Her toers ill be overgron ith thorns, her fortresses ith thistles and briers. She ill become a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches.
The desert creatures ill meet ith hyenas, and one ild goat ill call to another. There the night creature ill settle and find her place of repose.
There the ol ill make her nest; she ill lay and hatch her eggs and gather her brood under her shado. Even there the birds of prey ill gather, each ith its mate. \b
Search and read the scroll of the LORD: \b Not one of these ill go missing, not one ill lack her mate, because He has ordered it by His mouth, and He ill gather them by His Spirit.
He has allotted their portion; His hand has distributed it by measure. They ill possess it forever; they ill dell in it from generation to generation.
The ilderness and the land ill be glad; the desert ill rejoice and blossom like a rose.
It ill bloom profusely and rejoice ith joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon ill be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They ill see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God. \b
Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!
Say to those ith anxious hearts: “ Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God ill come ith vengeance. With divine retribution He ill come to save you.” \b
Then the eyes of the blind ill be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then the lame ill leap like a deer and the mute tongue ill shout for joy. For aters ill gush forth in the ilderness, and streams in the desert.
The parched ground ill become a pool, the thirsty land springs of ater. In the haunt here jackals once lay, there ill be grass and reeds and papyrus. \b
And there ill be a highay called the Way of Holiness. The unclean ill not travel it— only those ho alk in the Way— and fools ill not stray onto it.
No lion ill be there, and no vicious beast ill go up on it. Such ill not be found there, but the redeemed ill alk upon it.
So the redeemed of the LORD ill return and enter Zion ith singing, croned ith everlasting joy. Gladness and joy ill overtake them, and sorro and sighing ill flee.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, ith a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field. \b
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, ent out to him. \b
The Rabshakeh said to them, “ Tell Hezekiah that this is hat the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
You claim to have a strategy and strength for ar, but these are empty ords. In hom are you no trusting, that you have rebelled against me? \b
Look no, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that ill pierce the hand of anyone ho leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all ho trust in him.
But if you say to me, ’ We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One hose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, ’ You must orship before this altar’? \b
No, therefore, make a bargain ith my master, the king of Assyria. I ill give you to thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
For ho can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants hen you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
So no, as it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ’ Go up against this land and destroy it.’” \b
Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, “ Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since e understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebre in the hearing of the people on the all.” \b

But the Rabshakeh replied, “ Has my master sent me to speak these ords only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the all, ho are destined ith you to eat their on dung and drink their on urine?” \b
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebre: “ Hear the ords of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is hat the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD hen he says, ’ The LORD ill surely deliver us; this city ill not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’ \b

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is hat the king of Assyria says: Make peace ith me and come out to me. Then every one of you ill eat from his on vine and his on fig tree, and drink ater from his on cistern,
until I come and take you aay to a land like your on— a land of grain and ne ine, a land of bread and vineyards. \b
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you hen he says, ’ The LORD ill deliver us.’ Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand? Ho then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?” \b
But the people remained silent and did not anser a ord, for Hezekiah had commanded, “ Do not anser him.” \b
Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder came to Hezekiah ith their clothes torn, and they relayed to him the ords of the Rabshakeh.
On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.

This is hat the LORD says: \b “ The products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along ith the Sabeans, men of stature, ill come over to you and ill be yours; they ill trudge behind you; they ill come over in chains and bo don to you. “ Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, ho have been sustained from the omb, carried along since birth.

“ Go don and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground ithout a throne, O Daughter of Chaldea! For you ill no longer be called tender or delicate.

So take your stand ith your spells and ith your many sorceries, ith hich you have earied yourself from your youth. Perhaps you ill succeed; perhaps you ill inspire terror!

“ Listen to this, O house of Jacob, you ho are called by the name of Israel, ho have descended from the line of Judah, ho sear by the name of the LORD, ho invoke the God of Israel— but not in truth or righteousness—

I foretold the former things long ago; they came out of My mouth and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
For I kne that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.

You have heard these things; look at them all. Will you not acknoledge them? \b From no on I ill tell you of ne things, hidden things unknon to you.

You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open. For I kne ho deceitful you are; you have been called a rebel from birth. \b
For the sake of My name I ill delay My rath; for the sake of My praise I ill restrain it, so that you ill not be cut off.

Listen to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, hom I have called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last.
Surely My on hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; hen I summon them, they stand up together.
Come together, all of you, and listen: Which of the idols has foretold these things? The LORD’s chosen ally ill carry out His desire against Babylon, and His arm ill be against the Chaldeans.
I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he ill succeed in his mission. \b
Come near to Me and listen to this: \b From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it happened, I as there.” \b And no the Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit. \b
Thus says the LORD your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: \b “ I am the LORD your God, ho teaches you for your benefit, ho directs you in the ay you should go.
If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace ould have been like a river, and your righteousness like aves of the sea.
Your descendants ould have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains; their name ould never be cut off or eliminated from My presence.” \b
Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Declare it ith a shout of joy, proclaim it, let it go out to the ends of the earth, saying, “ The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!”
They did not thirst hen He led them through the deserts; He made ater flo for them from the rock; He split the rock, and ater gushed out. \b
“ There is no peace,” says the LORD, “ for the icked.”
Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples: \b The LORD called Me from the omb; from the body of My mother He named Me.
He made My mouth like a sharp sord; He hid Me in the shado of His hand. He made Me like a polished arro; He hid Me in His quiver.

And no says the LORD, ho formed Me from the omb to be His Servant, to bring Jacob back to Him, that Israel might be gathered to Him— for I am honored in the sight of the LORD, and My God is My strength—

This is hat the LORD says: \b “ In the time of favor I ill anser You, and in the day of salvation I ill help You; I ill keep You and appoint You to be a covenant for the people, to restore the land, to apportion its desolate inheritances,

“ Can a oman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her omb? Even if she could forget, I ill not forget you!

Seek the LORD hile He may be found; call on Him hile He is near.

“ For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ays My ays,” \qr declares the LORD.
“ For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ays are higher than your ays and My thoughts than your thoughts.

This is hat the LORD says: \b “ Maintain justice and do hat is right, for My salvation is coming soon, and My righteousness ill be revealed.

Let no foreigner ho has joined himself to the LORD say, “ The LORD ill utterly exclude me from His people.” And let the eunuch not say, “ I am but a dry tree.” \b

Thus declares the Lord GOD, ho gathers the dispersed of Israel: \b “ I ill gather to them still others besides those already gathered.” \b
Come, all you beasts of the field; eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest.

“ Come, let me get the ine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorro ill be like today, only far better!”

“ But come here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes!
Whom are you mocking? At hom do you snarl and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of deceit,
ho burn ith lust among the oaks, under every luxuriant tree, ho slaughter your children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?

On a high and lofty hill you have made your bed, and there you ent up to offer sacrifices.

I ill expose your righteousness and your orks, and they ill not profit you.

“ Why have e fasted, and You have not seen? Why have e humbled ourselves, and You have not noticed?” \b “ Behold, on the day of your fast, you do as you please, and you oppress all your orkers.
