Then the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

Tell the Ammonites to hear the ord of the Lord GOD, for this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Because you exclaimed, “ Aha!” hen My sanctuary as profaned, hen the land of Israel as laid aste, and hen the house of Judah ent into exile,
therefore I ill indeed give you as a possession to the people of the East. They ill set up their camps and pitch their tents among you. They ill eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I ill make Rabbah a pasture for camels, and Ammon a resting place for sheep. Then you ill kno that I am the LORD.’ \b
For this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Because you clapped your hands and stomped your feet and rejoiced over the land of Israel ith a heart full of contempt,

therefore I ill indeed stretch out My hand against you and give you as plunder to the nations. I ill cut you off from the peoples and exterminate you from the countries. I ill destroy you, and you ill kno that I am the LORD.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Because Moab and Seir said, “ Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,”
therefore I ill indeed expose the flank of Moab beginning ith its frontier cities— Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim— the glory of the land.
I ill give it along ith the Ammonites as a possession to the people of the East, so that the Ammonites ill no longer be remembered among the nations.
So I ill execute judgments on Moab, and they ill kno that I am the LORD.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Because Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah, and in so doing incurred grievous guilt,
therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: I ill stretch out My hand against Edom and cut off from it both man and beast. I ill make it a asteland, and from Teman to Dedan they ill fall by the sord.
I ill take My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel, and they ill deal ith Edom according to My anger and rath. Then they ill kno My vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Because the Philistines acted in vengeance, taking vengeance ith malice of soul to destroy Judah ith ancient hostility,
therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: Behold, I ill stretch out My hand against the Philistines, and I ill cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant along the coast.
I ill execute great vengeance against them ith furious reproof. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD, hen I lay My vengeance upon them.’”
In the eleventh month of the telfth year, on the first day of the month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, ’ Aha! The gate to the nations is broken; it has sung open to me; no that she lies in ruins I ill be filled,’
therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, O Tyre, I am against you, and I ill raise up many nations against you, as the sea brings up its aves.
They ill destroy the alls of Tyre and demolish her toers. I ill scrape the soil from her and make her a bare rock.
She ill become a place to spread nets in the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She ill become plunder for the nations,
and the villages on her mainland ill be slain by the sord. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD.’ \b
For this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Behold, I ill bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, ith horses and chariots, ith cavalry and a great company of troops.
He ill slaughter the villages of your mainland ith the sord; he ill set up siege orks against you, build a ramp to your alls, and raise his shields against you.
He ill direct the blos of his battering rams against your alls and tear don your toers ith his axes.
His multitude of horses ill cover you in their dust. \b
The hooves of his horses ill trample all your streets. He ill slaughter your people ith the sord, and your mighty pillars ill fall to the ground.
They ill plunder your ealth and pillage your merchandise. They ill demolish your alls, tear don your beautiful homes, and thro your stones and timber and soil into the ater. \b
So I ill silence the sound of your songs, and the music of your lyres ill no longer be heard.
I ill make you a bare rock, and you ill become a place to spread the fishing nets. You ill never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says to Tyre: ’ Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your donfall, hen the ounded groan at the slaughter in your midst? \b

All the princes of the sea ill descend from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. Clothed ith terror, they ill sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled over you.
Then they ill lament for you, saying, \b “Ho you have perished, O city of renon inhabited by seafaring men— she ho as poerful on the sea, along ith her people, ho imposed terror on all peoples!
No the coastlands tremble on the day of your donfall; the islands in the sea are dismayed by your demise.”’ \b
For this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ When I make you a desolate city like other deserted cities, and hen I raise up the deep against you so that the mighty aters cover you,

then I ill bring you don ith those ho descend to the Pit, to the people of antiquity. I ill make you dell in the earth belo like the ancient ruins, ith those ho descend to the Pit, so that you ill no longer be inhabited or set in splendor in the land of the living.
I ill make you an object of horror, and you ill be no more. You ill be sought, but ill never be found,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
Then the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ No you, son of man, take up a lament for Tyre.
Tell Tyre, ho dells at the gateay to the sea, merchant of the peoples on many coasts, that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b You have said, O Tyre, ’ I am perfect in beauty.’
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders perfected your beauty.
They constructed all your planking ith cypress from Senir. They took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; of ood from the coasts of Cyprus they made your deck, inlaid ith ivory.
Of embroidered fine linen from Egypt they made your sail, hich served as your banner. Of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah they made your aning. \b
The men of Sidon and Arvad ere your oarsmen. Your men of skill, O Tyre, ere there as your captains.
The elders of Gebal ere aboard as shiprights, repairing your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came alongside to barter for your merchandise. \b
Men of Persia, Lydia, and Put served as arriors in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your alls; they gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and Helech manned your alls all around, and the men of Gammad ere in your toers. They hung their shields around your alls; they perfected your beauty. \b \li1
Tarshish as your merchant because of your great ealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your ares. \b \li1
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech ere your merchants. They exchanged slaves and bronze utensils for your merchandise. \b \li1
The men of Beth-togarmah exchanged horses, ar horses, and mules for your ares. \b \li1
The men of Dedan ere your clients; many coastlands ere your market; they paid you ith ivory tusks and ebony. \b \li1
Aram as your customer because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered ork, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your ares. \b \li1
Judah and the land of Israel traded ith you; they exchanged heat from Minnith, cakes and honey, oil and balm for your merchandise. \b \li1
Because of your many products and your great ealth of goods, Damascus traded ith you ine from Helbon, ool from Zahar,
and casks of ine from Izal for your ares. Wrought iron, cassia, and seet cane ere exchanged for your merchandise. \b \li1
Dedan as your merchant in saddlecloths for riding. \b \li1
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar ere your customers, trading in lambs, rams, and goats. \b \li1
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded ith you; for your ares they exchanged gold, the finest of all spices, and precious stones. \b \li1
Haran, Canneh, and Eden traded ith you, and so did the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad.
In your marketplace they traded ith you fine garments of blue, embroidered ork, and multicolored rugs ith cords tightly tisted and knotted. \b
The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise. And you ere filled ith heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.
Your oarsmen have brought you onto the high seas, but the east ind ill shatter you in the heart of the sea.

Your ealth, ares, and merchandise, your sailors, captains, and shiprights, your merchants and all the arriors ithin you, ith all the other people on board, ill sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your donfall. \b
The countryside ill shake hen your sailors cry out.
All ho handle the oars ill abandon their ships. The sailors and all the captains of the sea ill stand on the shore.
They ill raise their voices for you and cry out bitterly. They ill thro dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They ill shave their heads for you and rap themselves in sackcloth. They ill eep over you ith anguish of soul and bitter mourning. \b
As they ail and mourn over you, they ill take up a lament for you: \b ’ Who as ever like Tyre, silenced in the middle of the sea?
When your ares ent out to sea, you satisfied many nations. You enriched the kings of the earth ith your abundant ealth and merchandise.
No you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the aters; your merchandise and the people among you have gone don ith you.
All the people of the coastlands are appalled over you. Their kings shudder ith fear; their faces are contorted.
Those ho trade among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and ill be no more.’”
And the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,

“ Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b Your heart is proud, and you have said, ’ I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the sea.’ Yet you are a man and not a god, though you have regarded your heart as that of a god. \b
Behold, you are iser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you!
By your isdom and understanding you have gained your ealth and amassed gold and silver for your treasuries.
By your great skill in trading you have increased your ealth, but your heart has gron proud because of it. \b
Therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b Because you regard your heart as the heart of a god,
behold, I ill bring foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They ill dra their sords against the beauty of your isdom and ill defile your splendor.
They ill bring you don to the Pit, and you ill die a violent death in the heart of the seas. \b
Will you still say, ’ I am a god,’ in the presence of those ho slay you? You ill be only a man, not a god, in the hands of those ho ound you.
You ill die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners. \b For I have spoken, \qr declares the Lord GOD.” \b
Again the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, take up a lament for the king of Tyre and tell him that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b ’ You ere the seal of perfection, full of isdom and perfect in beauty.

You ere in Eden, the garden of God. Every kind of precious stone adorned you: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald. Your mountings and settings ere crafted in gold, prepared on the day of your creation. \b
You ere anointed as a guardian cherub, for I had ordained you. You ere on the holy mountain of God; you alked among the fiery stones.
From the day you ere created you ere blameless in your ays— until ickedness as found in you. \b
By the vastness of your trade, you ere filled ith violence, and you sinned. So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you, O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones.
Your heart gre proud of your beauty; you corrupted your isdom because of your splendor; so I cast you to the earth; I made you a spectacle before kings. \b

By the multitude of your iniquities and the dishonesty of your trading you have profaned your sanctuaries. So I made fire come from ithin you, and it consumed you. I reduced you to ashes on the ground in the eyes of all ho sa you.
All the nations ho kno you are appalled over you. You have come to a horrible end and ill be no more.’” \b
Then the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, set your face against Sidon and prophesy against her.

And you are to declare that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b ’ Behold, I am against you, O Sidon, and I ill be glorified ithin you. They ill kno that I am the LORD hen I execute judgments against her and demonstrate My holiness through her.
I ill send a plague against her and shed blood in her streets; the slain ill fall ithin her, hile the sord is against her on every side. \b Then they ill kno that I am the LORD. \b
For the people of Israel ill no longer face a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all around them ho treat them ith contempt. Then they ill kno that I am the Lord GOD.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among hom they have been scattered, I ill sho Myself holy among them in the sight of the nations. \b

And there they ill dell securely, build houses, and plant vineyards. They ill dell securely hen I execute judgments against all those around them ho treat them ith contempt. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD their God.’”
In the tenth year, on the telfth day of the tenth month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

Speak to him and tell him that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b Behold, I am against you, O Pharaoh king of Egypt, O great monster ho lies among his rivers, ho says, ’ The Nile is mine; I made it myself.’ \b
But I ill put hooks in your jas and cause the fish of your streams to cling to your scales. I ill haul you up out of your rivers, and all the fish of your streams ill cling to your scales.

I ill leave you in the desert, you and all the fish of your streams. You ill fall on the open field and ill not be taken aay or gathered for burial. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the air.
Then all the people of Egypt ill kno that I am the LORD. \b For you ere only a staff of reeds to the house of Israel.
When Israel took hold of you ith their hands, you splintered, tearing all their shoulders; hen they leaned on you, you broke, and their backs ere renched. \b
Therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: I ill bring a sord against you and cut off from you man and beast.
The land of Egypt ill become a desolate asteland. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD. \b
therefore I am against you and against your rivers. I ill turn the land of Egypt into a ruin, a desolate asteland from Migdol to Syene, and as far as the border of Cush.
No foot of man or beast ill pass through, and it ill be uninhabited for forty years. \b

I ill make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities ill lie desolate for forty years among the ruined cities. And I ill disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries. \b
For this is hat the Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I ill gather the Egyptians from the nations to hich they ere scattered.
I ill restore Egypt from captivity and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin. There they ill be a loly kingdom. \b
Egypt ill be the loliest of kingdoms and ill never again exalt itself above the nations. For I ill diminish Egypt so that it ill never again rule over the nations.
Egypt ill never again be an object of trust for the house of Israel, but ill remind them of their iniquity in turning to the Egyptians. Then they ill kno that I am the Lord GOD.” \b
In the tenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,

“ Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to labor strenuously against Tyre. Every head as made bald and every shoulder made ra. But he and his army received no ages from Tyre for the labor they expended on it. \b

Therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: I ill give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, ho ill carry off its ealth, seize its spoil, and remove its plunder. This ill be the ages for his army.
I have given him the land of Egypt as the reard for his labor, because it as done for Me, declares the Lord GOD. \b
In that day I ill cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I ill open your mouth to speak among them. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD.”
Again the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, prophesy and declare that this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b Wail, ’ Alas for that day!’
For the day is near, the Day of the LORD is near. It ill be a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations. \b
A sord ill come against Egypt, and there ill be anguish in Cush hen the slain fall in Egypt, its ealth is taken aay, and its foundations are torn don.
Cush, Put, and Lud, and all the various peoples, as ell as Libya and the men of the covenant land, ill fall ith Egypt by the sord. \b
For this is hat the LORD says: \b The allies of Egypt ill fall, and her proud strength ill collapse. From Migdol to Syene they ill fall by the sord ithin her, \qr declares the Lord GOD.
They ill be desolate among desolate lands, and their cities ill lie among ruined cities. \b
Then they ill kno that I am the LORD hen I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are shattered. \b \li1
On that day messengers ill go out from Me in ships to frighten Cush out of complacency. Anguish ill come upon them on the day of Egypt’s doom. For it is indeed coming. \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: \b I ill put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people ith him, the most ruthless of the nations, ill be brought in to destroy the land. They ill dra their sords against Egypt and fill the land ith the slain.
I ill make the streams dry up and sell the land to the icked. By the hands of foreigners I ill bring desolation upon the land and everything in it. \qr I, the LORD, have spoken. \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: \b I ill destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There ill no longer be a prince in Egypt, and I ill instill fear in that land. \b
I ill lay aste Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgment on Thebes.
I ill pour out My rath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the crods of Thebes.
I ill set fire to Egypt, Pelusium ill rithe in anguish, Thebes ill be split open, and Memphis ill face daily distress. \b
The young men of On and Pi-beseth ill fall by the sord, and those cities ill go into captivity.
The day ill be darkened in Tahpanhes hen I break the yoke of Egypt and her proud strength comes to an end. A cloud ill cover her, and her daughters ill go into captivity. \b
So I ill execute judgment on Egypt, and they ill kno that I am the LORD.” \b
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. See, it has not been bound up for healing, or splinted for strength to hold the sord. \b
Therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I ill break his arms, both the strong one and the one already broken, and ill make the sord fall from his hand.
I ill disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands. \b
I ill strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king and place My sord in his hand, but I ill break the arms of Pharaoh, ho ill groan before him like a mortally ounded man.
I ill strengthen the arms of Babylon’s king, but Pharaoh’s arms ill fall limp. \b
I ill disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands. Then they ill kno that I am the LORD.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: \b ’ Who can be compared to your greatness?
Look at Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, ith beautiful branches that shaded the forest. It toered on high; its top as among the clouds.
The aters made it gro; the deep springs made it tall, directing their streams all around its base and sending their channels to all the trees of the field. \b
Therefore it toered higher than all the trees of the field. Its branches multiplied, and its boughs gre long as it spread them out because of the abundant aters.
All the birds of the air nested in its branches, and all the beasts of the field gave birth beneath its boughs; all the great nations lived in its shade. \b
It as beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its limbs, for its roots extended to abundant aters.
The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it; the cypresses could not compare ith its branches, nor the plane trees match its boughs. No tree in the garden of God could compare ith its beauty.
I made it beautiful ith its many branches, the envy of all the trees of Eden, hich ere in the garden of God.’ \b
Therefore this is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ Since it became great in height and set its top among the clouds, and it gre proud on account of its height,
I delivered it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal ith it according to its ickedness. I have banished it. \b

Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it don and left it. Its branches have fallen on the mountains and in every valley; its boughs lay broken in all the earth’s ravines. And all the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it. \b
All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field lived among its boughs.

This happened so that no other trees by the aters ould become great in height and set their tops among the clouds, and no other ell-atered trees ould reach them in height. For they have all been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the mortals ho descend to the Pit.’ \b

This is hat the Lord GOD says: ’ On the day it as brought don to Sheol, I caused mourning. I covered the deep because of it; I held back its rivers; its abundant aters ere restrained. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.
I made the nations quake at the sound of its donfall, hen I cast it don to Sheol ith those ho descend to the Pit. \b
They too descended ith it to Sheol, to those slain by the sord. As its allies they had lived in its shade among the nations. \b

Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You also ill be brought don to the depths of the earth to be ith the trees of Eden. You ill lie among the uncircumcised, ith those slain by the sord. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD.’”
In the telfth year, on the first day of the telfth month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,

“ Son of man, take up a lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: \b ’ You are like a lion among the nations; you are like a monster in the seas. You thrash about in your rivers, churning up the aters ith your feet and muddying the streams.’ \b
This is hat the Lord GOD says: \b ’ I ill spread My net over you ith a company of many peoples, and they ill dra you up in My net.
I ill abandon you on the land and hurl you into the open field. I ill cause all the birds of the air to settle upon you, and all the beasts of the earth to eat their fill of you.
I ill put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys ith your remains.
I ill drench the land ith the flo of your blood, all the ay to the mountains— the ravines ill be filled. \b
When I extinguish you, I ill cover the heavens and darken their stars. I ill cover the sun ith a cloud, and the moon ill not give its light.
All the shining lights in the heavens I ill darken over you, and I ill bring darkness upon your land,’ \qr declares the Lord GOD.
’ I ill trouble the hearts of many peoples, hen I bring about your destruction among the nations, in countries you do not kno.

I ill cause many peoples to be appalled over you, and their kings ill shudder in horror because of you hen I brandish My sord before them. On the day of your donfall each of them ill tremble every moment for his life.’ \b
For this is hat the Lord GOD says: \b ’ The sord of the king of Babylon ill come against you!
I ill make your hordes fall by the sords of the mighty, the most ruthless of all nations. They ill ravage the pride of Egypt and all her multitudes ill be destroyed.
I ill slaughter all her cattle beside the abundant aters. No human foot ill muddy them again, and no cattle hooves ill disturb them.
Then I ill let her aters settle and ill make her rivers flo like oil,’ \qr declares the Lord GOD.
’ When I make the land of Egypt a desolation and empty it of all that filled it, hen I strike don all ho live there, then they ill kno that I am the LORD.’
This is the lament they ill chant for her; the daughters of the nations ill chant it. Over Egypt and all her multitudes they ill chant it, declares the Lord GOD.” \b
In the telfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, ail for the multitudes of Egypt, and consign her and the daughters of the mighty nations to the depths of the earth ith those ho descend to the Pit: \b
Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go don and be placed ith the uncircumcised!
They ill fall among those slain by the sord. The sord is appointed! Let them drag her aay along ith all her multitudes. \b
Mighty chiefs ill speak from the midst of Sheol about Egypt and her allies: ’ They have come don and lie ith the uncircumcised, ith those slain by the sord.’ \b
Assyria is there ith her hole company; her graves are all around her. All of them are slain, fallen by the sord.
Her graves are set in the depths of the Pit, and her company is all around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sord— those ho once spread terror in the land of the living. \b

Elam is there ith all her multitudes around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sord— those ho ent don uncircumcised to the earth belo, ho once spread their terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace ith those ho descend to the Pit.

Among the slain they prepare a resting place for Elam ith all her hordes, ith her graves all around her. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sord, although their terror as once spread in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace ith those ho descend to the Pit. They are placed among the slain. \b
Meshech and Tubal are there ith all their multitudes, ith their graves all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sord, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.

They do not lie don ith the fallen arriors of old, ho ent don to Sheol ith their eapons of ar, hose sords ere placed under their heads, hose shields rested on their bones, although the terror of the mighty as once in the land of the living.
But you too ill be shattered and lie don among the uncircumcised, ith those slain by the sord. \b
Edom is there, and all her kings and princes, ho despite their might are laid among those slain by the sord. They lie don ith the uncircumcised, ith those ho descend to the Pit. \b

All the leaders of the north and all the Sidonians are there; they ent don in disgrace ith the slain, despite the terror of their might. They lie uncircumcised ith those slain by the sord and bear their shame ith those ho descend to the Pit. \b
Pharaoh ill see them and be comforted over all his multitude— Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sord, \qr declares the Lord GOD.
For I ill spread My terror in the land of the living, so that Pharaoh and all his multitude ill be laid to rest among the uncircumcised, ith those slain by the sord, \qr declares the Lord GOD.”
Again the ord of the LORD came to me, saying,
“ Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: ’ Suppose I bring the sord against a land, and the people of that land choose a man from among them, appointing him as their atchman,
and he sees the sord coming against that land and blos the ram’s horn to arn the people. \b
Then if anyone hears the sound of the horn but fails to heed the arning, and the sord comes and takes him aay, his blood ill be on his on head.
Since he heard the sound of the horn but failed to heed the arning, his blood ill be on his on head. If he had heeded the arning, he ould have saved his life. \b

But if the atchman sees the sord coming and fails to blo the horn to arn the people, and the sord comes and takes aay a life, then that one ill be taken aay in his iniquity, but I ill hold the atchman accountable for his blood.’ \b
As for you, O son of man, I have made you a atchman for the house of Israel; so hear the ord from My mouth and give them the arning from Me.

If I say to the icked, ’ O icked man, you ill surely die,’ but you do not speak out to dissuade him from his ay, then that icked man ill die in his iniquity, yet I ill hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you arn the icked man to turn from his ay, and he does not turn from it, he ill die in his iniquity, but you ill have saved your life. \b
No as for you, son of man, tell the house of Israel that this is hat they have said: ’ Our transgressions and our sins are heavy upon us, and e are asting aay because of them! Ho can e live?’ \b

Say to them: ’ As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the icked, but rather that the icked should turn from their ays and live. Turn! Turn from your evil ays! For hy should you die, O house of Israel?’ \b

Therefore, son of man, say to your people: ’ The righteousness of the righteous man ill not deliver him in the day of his transgression; neither ill the ickedness of the icked man cause him to stumble on the day he turns from his ickedness. Nor ill the righteous man be able to survive by his righteousness on the day he sins.’ \b

But Paul ansered, “ I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking ords of truth and sobriety.

Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that hich is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

This is also hy you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, ho devote themselves to their ork.
Pay everyone hat you oe him: taxes to hom taxes are due, revenue to hom revenue is due, respect to hom respect is due, honor to hom honor is due. \b
Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he ho loves his neighbor has fulfilled the la.
The commandments “ Do not commit adultery,” “ Do not murder,” “ Do not steal,” “ Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
Love does no rong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the la. \b
And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to ake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer no than hen e first believed.
The night is nearly over; the day has dran near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

Accept him hose faith is eak, ithout passing judgment on his opinions.
For one person has faith to eat all things, hile another, ho is eak, eats only vegetables.
The one ho eats everything must not belittle the one ho does not, and the one ho does not eat everything must not judge the one ho does, for God has accepted him.
Who are you to judge someone else’ s servant? To his on master he stands or falls. And he ill stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand. \b
One person regards a certain day above the others, hile someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his on mind.
He ho observes a special day does so to the Lord; he ho eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he ho abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God. \b
For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
If e live, e live to the Lord, and if e die, e die to the Lord. So hether e live or die, e belong to the Lord.
For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living. \b
Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or hy do you belittle your brother? For e ill all stand before God’s judgment seat.

Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s ay. \b
I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

Do not allo hat you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

So then, let us pursue hat leads to peace and to mutual edification.

Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the ill of God, and our brother Sosthenes, \b

I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you ise enough to arbitrate beteen his brothers?
Instead, one brother goes to la against another, and this in front of unbelievers! \b
The very fact that you have lasuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be ronged? Why not rather be cheated?
Instead, you yourselves cheat and do rong, even against your on brothers! \b
Do you not kno that the icked ill not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men ho submit to or perform homosexual acts,
nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor sindlers, ill inherit the kingdom of God.
And that is hat some of you ere. But you ere ashed, you ere sanctified, you ere justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God. \b
“ Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “ Everything is permissible for me,” but I ill not be mastered by anything.
“ Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God ill destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
By His poer God raised the Lord from the dead, and He ill raise us also. \b
Do you not kno that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them ith a prostitute? Never!
Or don’ t you kno that he ho unites himself ith a prostitute is one ith her in body? For it is said, “ The to ill become one flesh.”
But he ho unites himself ith the Lord is one ith Him in spirit. \b
Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he ho sins sexually sins against his on body.
Do you not kno that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit ho is in you, hom you have received from God? You are not your on;
you ere bought at a price. Therefore glorify God ith your body.
No for the matters you rote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.
But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his on ife, and each oman her on husband. \b
The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his ife, and likeise the ife to her husband.
The ife does not have authority over her on body, but the husband. Likeise the husband does not have authority over his on body, but the ife. \b

Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan ill not tempt you through your lack of self-control.
I say this as a concession, not as a command.
I ish that all men ere as I am. But each man has his on gift from God; one has this gift, another has that. \b
No to the unmarried and idos I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.
But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn ith passion. \b
To the married I give this command ( not I, but the Lord): A ife must not separate from her husband.
But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his ife. \b
To the rest I say this ( I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving ife and she is illing to live ith him, he must not divorce her.
And if a oman has an unbelieving husband and he is illing to live ith her, she must not divorce him.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing ife, and the unbelieving ife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherise your children ould be unclean, but no they are holy. \b
But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
Ho do you kno, ife, hether you ill save your husband? Or ho do you kno, husband, hether you ill save your ife? \b
Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to hich God has called him. This is hat I prescribe in all the churches.
Was a man already circumcised hen he as called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised hen called? He should not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is hat counts. \b
Each one should remain in the situation he as in hen he as called.
Were you a slave hen you ere called? Do not let it concern you— but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
For he ho as a slave hen he as called by the Lord is the Lord’ s freedman. Conversely, he ho as a free man hen he as called is Christ’ s slave. \b
You ere bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.
Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he as in hen God called him. \b
No about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one ho by the Lord’ s mercy is trustorthy.
Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.
Are you committed to a ife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a ife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those ho marry ill face troubles in this life, and I ant to spare you this. \b
What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From no on those ho have ives should live as if they had none;
those ho eep, as if they did not; those ho are joyful, as if they ere not; those ho make a purchase, as if they had nothing;
and those ho use the things of this orld, as if not dependent on them. For this orld in its present form is passing aay. \b
I ant you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the ork of the Lord, ho he can please the Lord.
But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this orld, ho he can please his ife,

and his interests are divided. The unmarried oman or virgin is concerned about the ork of the Lord, ho she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married oman is concerned about the affairs of this orld, ho she can please her husband. \b
I am saying this for your on good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord. \b
Hoever, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toard his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he ishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.
But the man ho is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, ith control over his ill and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he ill do ell. \b
So then, he ho marries the virgin does ell, but he ho does not marry her does even better. \b
A ife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she ishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
In my judgment, hoever, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
No about food sacrificed to idols: We kno that e all have knoledge. Knoledge puffs up, but love builds up.
The one ho thinks he knos something does not yet kno as he ought to kno.
But the one ho loves God is knon by God. \b
So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We kno that an idol is nothing at all in the orld, and that there is no God but one.
For even if there are so-called gods, hether in heaven or on earth ( as there are many so-called gods and lords),
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from hom all things came and for hom e exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through hom all things came and through hom e exist. \b
But not everyone has this knoledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it ere sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is eak, it is defiled.
But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no orse if e do not eat, and no better if e do. \b
Be careful, hoever, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the eak.
For if someone ith a eak conscience sees you ho are ell informed eating in an idol’ s temple, ill he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
So this eak brother, for hom Christ died, is destroyed by your knoledge.
By sinning against your brothers in this ay and ounding their eak conscience, you sin against Christ. \b
Therefore, if hat I eat causes my brother to stumble, I ill never eat meat again, so that I ill not cause him to stumble.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my orkmanship in the Lord?
Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord. \b
This is my defense to those ho scrutinize me:
Have e no right to food and to drink?
Have e no right to take along a believing ife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’ s brothers and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles ho must ork for a living? \b
Who serves as a soldier at his on expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk? \b
Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’ t the La say the same thing?
For it is ritten in the La of Moses: “ Do not muzzle an ox hile it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
Isn’ t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this as ritten for us, because hen the ploman plos and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest. \b
If e have son spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?
If others have this right to your support, shouldn’ t e have it all the more? But e did not exercise this right. Instead, e put up ith anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ. \b
Do you not kno that those ho ork in the temple eat of its food, and those ho serve at the altar partake of its offerings?
In the same ay, the Lord has prescribed that those ho preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not riting this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I ould rather die than let anyone nullify my boast. \b
Yet hen I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reard. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted ith a responsibility.
What then is my reard? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it. \b
Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to in as many as possible.
To the Jes I became like a Je, to in the Jes. To those under the la I became like one under the la ( though I myself am not under the la), to in those under the la.
To those ithout the la I became like one ithout the la ( though I am not outside the la of God but am under the la of Christ), to in those ithout the la.
To the eak I became eak, to in the eak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some. \b
I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings. \b
Do you not kno that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a ay as to take the prize.
Everyone ho competes in the games trains ith strict discipline. They do it for a cron that is perishable, but e do it for a cron that is imperishable.
Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

I do not ant you to be unaare, brothers, that our forefathers ere all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

They all ate the same spiritual food
and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock as Christ.
Nevertheless, God as not pleased ith most of them, for they ere struck don in the ilderness. \b
These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and ere killed by snakes.
And do not complain, as some of them did, and ere killed by the destroying angel. \b
No these things happened to them as examples and ere ritten don as arnings for us, on hom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
So the one ho thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

No temptation has seized you except hat is common to man. And God is faithful; He ill not let you be tempted beyond hat you can bear. But hen you are tempted, He ill also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it. \b
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves hat I say.
Is not the cup of blessing that e bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that e break a participation in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, e ho are many are one body; for e all partake of the one loaf. \b
Consider the people of Israel: Are not those ho eat the sacrifices fello partakers in the altar?
Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not ant you to be participants ith demons.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.
Are e trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are e stronger than He? \b
“ Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “ Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
No one should seek his on good, but the good of others. \b
Eat anything sold in the meat market ithout raising questions of conscience,
for, “ The earth is the Lord’ s, and the fullness thereof.” \b
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you ant to go, eat anything set before you ithout raising questions of conscience.
But if someone tells you, “ This food as offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one ho told you and for the sake of conscience—
the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your on. For hy should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?
If I partake in the meal ith thankfulness, hy am I denounced because of that for hich I give thanks? \b
So hether you eat or drink or hatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
Do not become a stumbling block, hether to Jes or Greeks or the church of God—
as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my on good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ. \b
No I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.
But I ant you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the oman is man, and the head of Christ is God. \b
Every man ho prays or prophesies ith his head covered dishonors his head.
And every oman ho prays or prophesies ith her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head ere shaved.
If a oman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a oman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head. \b
A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the oman is the glory of man.
For man did not come from oman, but oman from man.
Neither as man created for oman, but oman for man.
For this reason a oman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels. \b
In the Lord, hoever, oman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of oman.
For just as oman came from man, so also man is born of oman. But everything comes from God. \b
Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a oman to pray to God ith her head uncovered?
Doesn’ t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
but that if a oman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone is inclined to dispute this, e have no other practice, nor do the churches of God. \b
In the folloing instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.
First of all, I hear that hen you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
And indeed, there must be differences among you to sho hich of you are approved. \b
No then, hen you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.
For as you eat, each of you goes ahead ithout sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
Don’ t you have your on homes in hich to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those ho have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I ill not! \b
For I received from the Lord hat I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He as betrayed, took bread,
and hen He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “ This is My body, hich is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
In the same ay, after supper He took the cup, saying, “ This cup is the ne covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’ s death until He comes. \b
Therefore, hoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unorthy manner ill be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.
For anyone ho eats and drinks ithout recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
That is hy many among you are eak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep. \b
No if e judged ourselves properly, e ould not come under judgment.
But hen e are judged by the Lord, e are being disciplined so that e ill not be condemned ith the orld. \b
So, my brothers, hen you come together to eat, ait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that hen you come together it ill not result in judgment. And hen I come, I ill give instructions about the remaining matters.
No about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not ant you to be uninformed.
You kno that hen you ere pagans, you ere influenced and led astray to mute idols.
Therefore I inform you that no one ho is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “ Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “ Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit. \b
There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are different ministries, but the same Lord.
There are different ays of orking, but the same God orks all things in all people. \b
No to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
To one there is given through the Spirit the message of isdom, to another the message of knoledge by the same Spirit,
to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,
to another the orking of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing beteen spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.
All these are the ork of one and the same Spirit, ho apportions them to each one as He determines. \b
The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is ith Christ.
For in one Spirit e ere all baptized into one body, hether Jes or Greeks, slave or free, and e ere all given one Spirit to drink. \b
For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.
If the foot should say, “ Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that ould not make it any less a part of the body.
And if the ear should say, “ Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that ould not make it any less a part of the body.
If the hole body ere an eye, here ould the sense of hearing be? If the hole body ere an ear, here ould the sense of smell be? \b
But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
If they ere all one part, here ould the body be?
As it is, there are many parts, but one body. \b
The eye cannot say to the hand, “ I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “ I do not need you.”
On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be eaker are indispensable,
and the parts e consider less honorable, e treat ith greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated ith special modesty,
hereas our presentable parts have no such need. \b
so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers ith it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices ith it. \b
No you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then orkers of miracles, and those ith gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all ork miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But eagerly desire the greater gifts. \b
If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knoledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing. \b
Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of rongs.
Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. \b
Love never fails. But here there are prophecies, they ill cease; here there are tongues, they ill be restrained; here there is knoledge, it ill be dismissed.
For e kno in part and e prophesy in part,
but hen the perfect comes, the partial passes aay. \b
When I as a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ays.
No e see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then e shall see face to face. No I kno in part; then I shall kno fully, even as I am fully knon. \b
And no these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.
For he ho speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
But he ho prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.
The one ho speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one ho prophesies edifies the church. \b

I ish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I ould rather have you prophesy. He ho prophesies is greater than one ho speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified. \b
No, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, ho ill I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knoledge or prophecy or teaching?
Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, ho ill anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?
Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, ho ill prepare for battle?
So it is ith you. Unless you speak intelligible ords ith your tongue, ho ill anyone kno hat you are saying? You ill just be speaking into the air. \b
Assuredly, there are many different languages in the orld, yet none of them is ithout meaning.
If, then, I do not kno the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me. \b
It is the same ith you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.
Therefore, the one ho speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful. \b
What then shall I do? I ill pray ith my spirit, but I ill also pray ith my mind. I ill sing ith my spirit, but I ill also sing ith my mind.
Otherise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, ho can someone ho is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not kno hat you are saying?
You may be giving thanks ell enough, but the other one is not edified. \b
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the church, I ould rather speak five coherent ords to instruct others than ten thousand ords in a tongue. \b
Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
It is ritten in the La: \b “ By strange tongues and foreign lips I ill speak to this people, but even then they ill not listen to Me, says the Lord.” \b
Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, hoever, is for believers, not for unbelievers. \b
So if the hole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some ho are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, ill they not say that you are out of your minds?
But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in hile everyone is prophesying, he ill be convicted and called to account by all,
and the secrets of his heart ill be made knon. So he ill fall facedon and orship God, proclaiming, “ God is truly among you!” \b
What then shall e say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church. \b
If anyone speaks in a tongue, to, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.
But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God. \b
To or three prophets should speak, and the others should eigh carefully hat is said.
And if a revelation comes to someone ho is seated, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace— as in all the churches of the saints. \b
Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the la says.
If they ish to inquire about something, they are to ask their on husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a oman to speak in the church. \b
Did the ord of God originate ith you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknoledge that hat I am riting you is the Lord’ s command.
But if anyone ignores this, he himself ill be ignored. \b
So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
No, brothers, I ant to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, hich you received, and in hich you stand firm.
By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the ord I preached to you. Otherise, you have believed in vain. \b
For hat I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
that He as buried, that He as raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Telve.
After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of hom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth. \b
For I am the least of the apostles and am unorthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by the grace of God I am hat I am, and His grace to me as not in vain. No, I orked harder than all of them— yet not I, but the grace of God that as ith me.
Whether, then, it as I or they, this is hat e preach, and this is hat you believed. \b
But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, ho can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is orthless, and so is your faith.
In that case, e are also exposed as false itnesses about God. For e have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised. \b
For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
Then those also ho have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, e are to be pitied more than all men. \b
But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those ho have fallen asleep.
For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all ill be made alive.
But each in his on turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those ho belong to Him. \b
Then the end ill come, hen He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and poer.
For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For “ God has put everything under His feet.” No hen it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One ho put everything under Him.
And hen all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself ill be made subject to Him ho put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all. \b
If these things are not so, hat ill those do ho are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, hy are people baptized for them?
And hy do e endanger ourselves every hour?
I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
